Appendix D Online Linear Optimization with Drift Penalization: Proofs

This section proves the results for drift-penalized OLO from Section 4. Theorem 4.1 and Lemma 4.2 establish how P-FTRL and OMD control the standard regret ℜN​(u)=∑n=1N⟨cn,zn−u⟩\mathfrak{R}_{N}(u)=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\langle{c_{n},z_{n}-u}\rangle and the prediction drift 𝔇N=∑n=1N‖zn−λn−zn‖\mathfrak{D}_{N}=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\|z_{n-\lambda_{n}}\!-\!z_{n}\|. Given a non-increasing learning rate sequence {ηn}n=1N⊂(0,∞)\{\eta_{n}\}_{n=1}^{N}\subset(0,\infty) and initial point z1∈𝒦z_{1}\in\mathcal{K}, we consider the update rules

P-FTRL:zn+1\displaystyle\textnormal{P-FTRL}:\,\,z_{n+1} =argminz∈𝒦⟨∑m=1ncm,z⟩+∑m=1n1/ηm−1/ηm−12​‖zm−z‖2,\displaystyle=\textstyle\argmin_{z\in\mathcal{K}}\,\langle{\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{n}c_{m},\,z}\rangle+\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{n}\tfrac{1/\eta_{m}-1/\eta_{m-1}}{2}\left\|z_{m}-z\right\|^{2},
OMD:zn+1\displaystyle\textnormal{OMD}:\,\,z_{n+1} =argminz∈𝒦⟨cn,z⟩+1/ηn2​‖zn−z‖2,\displaystyle=\textstyle\argmin_{z\in\mathcal{K}}\,\langle{c_{n},\,z}\rangle+\tfrac{1/\eta_{n}}{2}\left\|z_{n}-z\right\|^{2},

with the convention 1/η0=01/\eta_{0}=0.

D.1 General results for FTRL and OMD

The following results are standard in the analysis of FTRL and OMD.

Theorem D.1 (Orabona (2019), adapted from Lemmas 7.1 and 7.8 for linear losses).

Let 𝒦⊂ℝk\mathcal{K}\subset\mathbb{R}^{k} be a convex compact set, let {ηn}n=1N⊂(0,∞)\{\eta_{n}\}_{n=1}^{N}\subset(0,\infty) be a non-increasing sequence, and let ψ1,…,ψN:ℝk→ℝ\psi_{1},\ldots,\psi_{N}:\mathbb{R}^{k}\to\mathbb{R} be differentiable functions such that each ψn\psi_{n} is (1/ηn)(1/\eta_{n})-strongly convex with respect to ∥⋅∥\|\cdot\| on 𝒦\mathcal{K}. Given loss vectors {cn}n=1N⊂ℝk\{c_{n}\}_{n=1}^{N}\subset\mathbb{R}^{k} and an initial point z1∈𝒦z_{1}\in\mathcal{K}, we can iteratively select unique minimizers zn+1=argminz∈𝒦{ψn​(z)+∑m=1n⟨cm,z⟩}z_{n+1}=\argmin_{z\in\mathcal{K}}\left\{\psi_{n}(z)+\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{n}\langle{c_{m},z}\rangle\right\}. For proximal regularizers ψn\psi_{n} such that zn∈argminz∈𝒦{ψn​(z)−ψn−1​(z)}z_{n}\in\argmin_{z\in\mathcal{K}}\{\psi_{n}(z)-\psi_{n-1}(z)\}, for all u∈𝒦u\in\mathcal{K}, it holds that

∑n=1N⟨cn,zn−u⟩≤ψN​(u)+∑n=1N(12​ηn​‖cn‖⋆2+ψn−1​(zn)−ψn​(zn)).\displaystyle\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\langle{c_{n},z_{n}-u}\rangle\leq\psi_{N}(u)+\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\eta_{n}\|c_{n}\|_{\star}^{2}+\psi_{n-1}(z_{n})-\psi_{n}(z_{n})\right).
Lemma D.2 (Stability lemma, modified version of Lemma A.2 in Qiu et al. (2025)).

Let 𝒦⊂ℝk\mathcal{K}\subset\mathbb{R}^{k} be a convex compact set. For i∈{0,1}i\in\{0,1\}, let function ϕi:ℝk→ℝ\phi_{i}:\mathbb{R}^{k}\to\mathbb{R} be differentiable and λi\lambda_{i}-strongly convex with respect to ∥.∥\|.\| on 𝒦\mathcal{K}. Consider zi∈argminx∈𝒦⟨wi,x⟩+ϕi​(x)z_{i}\in\argmin_{x\in\mathcal{K}}\langle{w_{i},\,x}\rangle+\phi_{i}(x). It holds that

λ0+λ12​‖z0−z1‖2≤⟨w0−w1,z1−z0⟩+(ϕ1​(z0)−ϕ0​(z0))−(ϕ1​(z1)−ϕ0​(z1)).\displaystyle\tfrac{\lambda_{0}+\lambda_{1}}{2}\left\|z_{0}-z_{1}\right\|^{2}\leq\langle{w_{0}-w_{1},\,z_{1}-z_{0}}\rangle+(\phi_{1}(z_{0})-\phi_{0}(z_{0}))-(\phi_{1}(z_{1})-\phi_{0}(z_{1})).
Proof.

For i∈{0,1}i\in\{0,1\}, let hi​(x)=⟨wi,x⟩+ϕi​(x)h_{i}(x)=\langle{w_{i},\,x}\rangle+\phi_{i}(x) denote the λi\lambda_{i}-strongly convex function minimized at point ziz_{i}. Therefore, by the strong convexity of hih_{i}, it holds that

hi​(z1−i)−hi​(zi)≥λi2​‖z1−i−zi‖2.\displaystyle h_{i}(z_{1-i})-h_{i}(z_{i})\geq\tfrac{\lambda_{i}}{2}\left\|z_{1-i}-z_{i}\right\|^{2}.

By summing the above inequality for both i∈{0,1}i\in\{0,1\}, we conclude

⟨w0−w1,z1−z0⟩+(ϕ1​(z0)−ϕ0​(z0))−(ϕ1​(z1)−ϕ0​(z1))\displaystyle\langle{w_{0}-w_{1},\,z_{1}-z_{0}}\rangle+(\phi_{1}(z_{0})-\phi_{0}(z_{0}))-(\phi_{1}(z_{1})-\phi_{0}(z_{1})) =h0​(z1)−h0​(z0)+h1​(z0)−h1​(z1)\displaystyle=h_{0}(z_{1})-h_{0}(z_{0})+h_{1}(z_{0})-h_{1}(z_{1})
≥λ0+λ12​‖z0−z1‖2.∎\displaystyle\geq\tfrac{\lambda_{0}+\lambda_{1}}{2}\left\|z_{0}-z_{1}\right\|^{2}.\qed
Lemma D.3 (Orabona (2019), adapted from Lemma 6.10 for linear losses).

Let 𝒦⊂ℝk\mathcal{K}\subset\mathbb{R}^{k} be a convex compact set. Consider function ψ:ℝk→ℝ\psi:\mathbb{R}^{k}\to\mathbb{R} that is proper, closed, differentiable, 11-strongly convex function with respect to ∥.∥\|.\| in 𝒦\mathcal{K}, with Bψ:ℝk×ℝk→ℝB_{\psi}:\mathbb{R}^{k}\times\mathbb{R}^{k}\to\mathbb{R} denoting its Bregman divergence, i.e., Bψ​(x,y)=ψ⁡(x)−ψ⁡(y)−⟨∇ψ​(y),x−y⟩B_{\psi}(x;y)=\psi(x)-\psi(y)-\langle{\nabla\psi(y),x-y}\rangle. Given {cn}n=1N⊂ℝk\{c_{n}\}_{n=1}^{N}\subset\mathbb{R}^{k}, non-increasing sequence {ηn}n=1N⊂(0,∞)\{\eta_{n}\}_{n=1}^{N}\subset(0,\infty), and z1∈𝒦z_{1}\in\mathcal{K}, we can iteratively select unique minimizers zn+1=argminz∈𝒦⟨z,cn⟩+1ηn​Bψ​(z,zn)z_{n+1}=\argmin_{z\in\mathcal{K}}\langle{z,c_{n}}\rangle+\frac{1}{\eta_{n}}B_{\psi}(z;z_{n}). Moreover, for all u∈𝒦u\in\mathcal{K} and n∈[N]n\in[N]:

ηn​⟨cn,xn−u⟩≤Bψ​(u,zn)−Bψ​(u,zn+1)+ηn22​‖cn‖⋆2.\displaystyle\eta_{n}\langle{c_{n},x_{n}-u}\rangle\leq B_{\psi}(u;z_{n})-B_{\psi}(u;z_{n+1})+\tfrac{\eta_{n}^{2}}{2}\|c_{n}\|_{\star}^{2}.
Theorem D.4 (OMD: Regret and Drift).

Under the assumptions of Lemma D.3, for all u∈𝒦u\in\mathcal{K}, it holds that

∑n=1N⟨cn,zn−u⟩≤∑n=1N(1ηn−1ηn−1)​Bψ​(u,zn)+12​∑n=1Nηn​‖cn‖⋆2.\displaystyle\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\langle{c_{n},z_{n}-u}\rangle\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}(\tfrac{1}{\eta_{n}}-\tfrac{1}{\eta_{n-1}})B_{\psi}(u;z_{n})+\tfrac{1}{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\eta_{n}\|c_{n}\|_{\star}^{2}.

Moreover, for all n∈[N−1]n\in[N-1], it holds that ‖zn+1−zn‖≤ηn​‖cn‖⋆\|z_{n+1}-z_{n}\|\leq\eta_{n}\|c_{n}\|_{\star}.

Proof.

For all u∈𝒦u\in\mathcal{K}, using Lemma D.3, we write

∑n=1N⟨cn,zn−u⟩\displaystyle\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\langle{c_{n},z_{n}-u}\rangle ≤∑n=1N(1ηn​Bψ​(u,zn)−1ηn​Bψ​(u,zn+1))+12​∑n=1Nηn​‖cn‖⋆2\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\left(\tfrac{1}{\eta_{n}}B_{\psi}(u;z_{n})-\tfrac{1}{\eta_{n}}B_{\psi}(u;z_{n+1})\right)+\tfrac{1}{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\eta_{n}\|c_{n}\|_{\star}^{2}
=∑n=1N(1ηn−1ηn−1)​Bψ​(u,zn)−1ηN​Bψ​(u,zN+1)+12​∑n=1Nηn​‖cn‖⋆2,\displaystyle=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}(\tfrac{1}{\eta_{n}}-\tfrac{1}{\eta_{n-1}})B_{\psi}(u;z_{n})-\tfrac{1}{\eta_{N}}B_{\psi}(u;z_{N+1})+\tfrac{1}{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\eta_{n}\|c_{n}\|_{\star}^{2},

where Bψ​(u,zN+1)≥0B_{\psi}(u;z_{N+1})\geq 0 for Bregman divergence. This concludes the proof of the regret bound.

Fix arbitrary n∈[N]n\in[N] and let ϕ0​(z)=1ηn​Bψ​(z,zn)\phi_{0}(z)=\frac{1}{\eta_{n}}B_{\psi}(z;z_{n}). Let g0=∇ϕ0​(zn)g_{0}=\nabla\phi_{0}(z_{n}) and g1=∇ϕ0​(zn+1)g_{1}=\nabla\phi_{0}(z_{n+1}). By the first-order optimality of zn=argminz∈𝒦{ϕ0​(z)}z_{n}=\argmin_{z\in\mathcal{K}}\{\phi_{0}(z)\} and zn+1=argminz∈𝒦{⟨z,cn⟩+ϕ0​(z)}z_{n+1}=\argmin_{z\in\mathcal{K}}\{\langle{z,c_{n}}\rangle+\phi_{0}(z)\}, we have

⟨g0,zn−zn+1⟩≤0and⟨cn+g1,zn−zn+1⟩≥0.\displaystyle\langle{g_{0},\,z_{n}-z_{n+1}}\rangle\leq 0\quad\text{and}\quad\langle{c_{n}+g_{1},\,z_{n}-z_{n+1}}\rangle\geq 0.

The monotonicity inequality for 1ηn\tfrac{1}{\eta_{n}}-strong convex ϕ0\phi_{0} yields ⟨g0−g1,zn−zn+1⟩≥1ηn​‖zn−zn+1‖2\langle{g_{0}-g_{1},\,z_{n}-z_{n+1}}\rangle\geq\tfrac{1}{\eta_{n}}\left\|z_{n}-z_{n+1}\right\|^{2}.
Combining these inequalities, we have

1ηn​‖zn−zn+1‖2\displaystyle\tfrac{1}{\eta_{n}}\left\|z_{n}-z_{n+1}\right\|^{2} ≤⟨g0−g1,zn−zn+1⟩\displaystyle\leq\langle{g_{0}-g_{1},\,z_{n}-z_{n+1}}\rangle
=⟨cn,zn−zn+1⟩+⟨g0,zn−zn+1⟩−⟨cn+g1,zn−zn+1⟩\displaystyle=\langle{c_{n},\,z_{n}-z_{n+1}}\rangle+\langle{g_{0},\,z_{n}-z_{n+1}}\rangle-\langle{c_{n}+g_{1},\,z_{n}-z_{n+1}}\rangle
≤‖cn‖⋆​‖zn−zn+1‖+0+0.\displaystyle\leq\left\|c_{n}\right\|_{\star}\left\|z_{n}-z_{n+1}\right\|+0+0.

Consequently, ‖zn−zn+1‖≤ηn​‖cn‖⋆\|z_{n}-z_{n+1}\|\leq\eta_{n}\|c_{n}\|_{\star}. ∎

D.2 Auxiliary Results for Drift Control of P-FTRL

Lemma D.5.

Let {zn}n=1T\{z_{n}\}_{n=1}^{T} denote predictions of P-FTRL (4). For all n∈[N]n\in[N] and λ∈[N−n]\lambda\in[N-n], it holds that

‖zn+λ−zn‖≤ηn+λ​‖∑m=nn+λ−1cm‖⋆+(1−ηn+λ/ηn)​D.\displaystyle\left\|z_{n+\lambda}-z_{n}\right\|\leq\eta_{n+\lambda}\,\|\textstyle\sum_{m=n}^{n+\lambda-1}c_{m}\|_{\star}+(1-\eta_{n+\lambda}/\eta_{n})D.

Moreover, it holds that ‖zn+1−zn‖≤ηn​‖cn‖⋆\left\|z_{n+1}-z_{n}\right\|\leq\eta_{n}\,\|c_{n}\|_{\star} for n∈[N−1]n\in[N-1].

Proof.

Let α1=1/η1\alpha_{1}=1/\eta_{1} and αn+1=1/ηn+1−1/ηn\alpha_{n+1}=1/\eta_{n+1}-1/\eta_{n} for n∈[N−1]n\in[N-1].

To apply Lemma D.2, consider the following vectors and functions

w0=∑m=1n−1cm,\displaystyle w_{0}=\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{n-1}c_{m}, ϕ0​(z)=∑m=1nαm2​‖z−zm‖2,\displaystyle\quad\phi_{0}(z)=\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{n}\tfrac{\alpha_{m}}{2}\left\|z-z_{m}\right\|^{2},
w1=∑m=1n+λ−1cm,\displaystyle w_{1}=\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{n+\lambda-1}c_{m}, ϕ1​(z)=∑m=1n+λαm2​‖z−zm‖2,\displaystyle\quad\phi_{1}(z)=\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{n+\lambda}\tfrac{\alpha_{m}}{2}\left\|z-z_{m}\right\|^{2},

so that zn=argminz∈𝒦⟨z,w0⟩+ϕ0​(z)z_{n}=\argmin_{z\in\mathcal{K}}\langle{z,w_{0}}\rangle+\phi_{0}(z) and zn+λ=argminz∈𝒦⟨z,w1⟩+ϕ1​(z)z_{n+\lambda}=\argmin_{z\in\mathcal{K}}\langle{z,w_{1}}\rangle+\phi_{1}(z), while ϕ0\phi_{0} and ϕ1\phi_{1} are 1/ηn1/\eta_{n} and 1/ηn+λ1/\eta_{n+\lambda}-strongly convex, respectively.

Applying Lemma D.2, we have

1ηn+λ+1ηn2​‖zn−zn+λ‖2\displaystyle\tfrac{\frac{1}{\eta_{n+\lambda}}+\frac{1}{\eta_{n}}}{2}\left\|z_{n}\!-\!z_{n+\lambda}\right\|^{2} ≤⟨∑m=nn+λ−1cm,zn−zn+λ⟩+∑m=n+1n+λαm2​(‖zn−zm‖2−‖zn+λ−zm‖2)\displaystyle\leq\langle{\textstyle\sum_{m=n}^{n+\lambda-1}c_{m},\,z_{n}\!-\!z_{n+\lambda}}\rangle+\textstyle\sum_{m=n+1}^{n+\lambda}\tfrac{\alpha_{m}}{2}\left(\left\|z_{n}-z_{m}\right\|^{2}-\left\|z_{n+\lambda}-z_{m}\right\|^{2}\right)
=⟨∑m=nn+λ−1cm,zn−zn+λ⟩+⟨∑m=n+1n+λαm2​(zn+zn+λ−2​zm),zn−zn+λ⟩\displaystyle=\langle{\textstyle\sum_{m=n}^{n+\lambda-1}c_{m},\,z_{n}\!-\!z_{n+\lambda}}\rangle+\langle{\textstyle\sum_{m=n+1}^{n+\lambda}\tfrac{\alpha_{m}}{2}(z_{n}\!+\!z_{n+\lambda}\!-\!2z_{m}),\,z_{n}\!-\!z_{n+\lambda}}\rangle
=⟨∑m=nn+λ−1cm,zn−zn+λ⟩+⟨∑m=n+1n+λαm​(zn−zm),zn−zn+λ⟩\displaystyle=\langle{\textstyle\sum_{m=n}^{n+\lambda-1}c_{m},\,z_{n}\!-\!z_{n+\lambda}}\rangle+\langle{\textstyle\sum_{m=n+1}^{n+\lambda}\alpha_{m}(z_{n}-z_{m}),\,z_{n}\!-\!z_{n+\lambda}}\rangle
−1ηn+λ−1ηn2​‖zn−zn+λ‖2.\displaystyle-\tfrac{\frac{1}{\eta_{n+\lambda}}-\frac{1}{\eta_{n}}}{2}\left\|z_{n}\!-\!z_{n+\lambda}\right\|^{2}.

Grouping terms containing ‖zn−zn+λ‖2\left\|z_{n}-z_{n+\lambda}\right\|^{2} on the left side and using Assumptions 2.1, we write

1ηn+λ​‖zn−zn+λ‖2\displaystyle\tfrac{1}{\eta_{n+\lambda}}\left\|z_{n}-z_{n+\lambda}\right\|^{2} ≤⟨∑m=nn+λ−1cm,zn−zn+λ⟩+⟨∑m=n+1n+λαm​(zn−zm),zn−zn+λ⟩\displaystyle\leq\langle{\textstyle\sum_{m=n}^{n+\lambda-1}c_{m},\,z_{n}-z_{n+\lambda}}\rangle+\langle{\textstyle\sum_{m=n+1}^{n+\lambda}\alpha_{m}(z_{n}-z_{m}),\,z_{n}-z_{n+\lambda}}\rangle
≤(‖∑m=nn+λ−1cm‖⋆+(1/ηn+λ−1/ηn)​D)​‖zn−zn+λ‖.\displaystyle\leq\left(\|\textstyle\sum_{m=n}^{n+\lambda-1}c_{m}\|_{\star}+(1/\eta_{n+\lambda}-1/\eta_{n})D\right)\,\left\|z_{n}-z_{n+\lambda}\right\|.

The first inequality immediately follows. Alternatively, for λ=1\lambda=1, we have

1ηn​‖zn−zn+1‖2\displaystyle\tfrac{1}{\eta_{n}}\left\|z_{n}-z_{n+1}\right\|^{2} =(1ηn+1−αn+1)​‖zn−zn+1‖2\displaystyle=(\tfrac{1}{\eta_{n+1}}-\alpha_{n+1})\left\|z_{n}-z_{n+1}\right\|^{2}
≤⟨cn,zn−zn+1⟩+⟨αn+1​(zn−zn+1),zn−zn+1⟩−αn+1​‖zn−zn+1‖2\displaystyle\leq\langle{c_{n},\,z_{n}-z_{n+1}}\rangle+\langle{\alpha_{n+1}(z_{n}-z_{n+1}),\,z_{n}-z_{n+1}}\rangle-\alpha_{n+1}\left\|z_{n}-z_{n+1}\right\|^{2}
=⟨cn,zn−zn+1⟩\displaystyle=\langle{c_{n},\,z_{n}-z_{n+1}}\rangle
≤‖cn‖⋆​‖zn−zn+1‖.\displaystyle\leq\|c_{n}\|_{\star}\,\|z_{n}-z_{n+1}\|.

The second result follows from this, concluding the proof. ∎

Lemma D.6.

For learning rates {ηn}n=1N\{\eta_{n}\}_{n=1}^{N} of P-FTRL (4), let Hη=∑n=1N(1−ηnηn−λn)H_{\eta}=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}(1-\tfrac{\eta_{n}}{\eta_{n-\lambda_{n}}}). Then,

Hη≤(maxn∈[N]⁡νn+1)​ln⁡(e​η1ηN)andHη≤max⁡∑m=nn+νnn∈[N]⁡ηmηN.\displaystyle H_{\eta}\leq(\textstyle\max_{n\in[N]}\nu_{n}+1)\ln\left(\tfrac{e\eta_{1}}{\eta_{N}}\right)\qquad\text{and}\qquad H_{\eta}\leq\frac{\max_{n\in[N]}\sum_{m=n}^{n+\nu_{n}}\eta_{m}}{\eta_{N}}.
Proof.

Let α1=1/η1>0\alpha_{1}=1/\eta_{1}>0 and αn+1=1/ηn+1−1/ηn≥0\alpha_{n+1}=1/\eta_{n+1}-1/\eta_{n}\geq 0 for n∈[N−1]n\in[N-1]. Then, we can write

Hη=∑n=1Nηn​(1ηn−1ηn−λn)\displaystyle H_{\eta}=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\eta_{n}\Bigl(\tfrac{1}{\eta_{n}}-\tfrac{1}{\eta_{n-\lambda_{n}}}\Bigr) =∑n=1Nηn∑m=1Nαm𝕀(n−λn<m≤n)\displaystyle=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\eta_{n}\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{N}\alpha_{m}\,\ind(n-\lambda_{n}<m\leq n)
=∑m=1Nαm∑n=1Nηn𝕀(n−λn<m≤n).\displaystyle=\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{N}\alpha_{m}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\eta_{n}\ind(n-\lambda_{n}<m\leq n).

Since the sequence {ηn}n=1N\{\eta_{n}\}_{n=1}^{N} is non-increasing and by Lemma 3.6,

∑n=1N𝕀(n−λn<m≤n)≤∑n=1N𝕀(n−λn≤m<n)+1=νm+1,\displaystyle\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\ind(n-\lambda_{n}<m\leq n)\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\ind(n-\lambda_{n}\leq m<n)+1=\nu_{m}+1,

we can further write, with νmax=maxn∈[N]⁡νn\nu_{\textnormal{max}}=\max_{n\in[N]}\nu_{n}:

Hη\displaystyle H_{\eta} ≤∑m=1Nαm​ηm​(νm+1)≤(νmax+1)​∑m=1Nαm​ηm\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{N}\alpha_{m}\eta_{m}\,(\nu_{m}+1)\leq(\nu_{\textnormal{max}}+1)\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{N}\alpha_{m}\eta_{m}
=(νmax+1)​∑m=1Nαm∑k=1mαk≤(νmax+1)​ln⁡(e​η1ηN),\displaystyle=(\nu_{\textnormal{max}}+1)\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{N}\frac{\alpha_{m}}{\sum_{k=1}^{m}\alpha_{k}}\leq(\nu_{\textnormal{max}}+1)\ln\left(\tfrac{e\eta_{1}}{\eta_{N}}\right),

where the final inequality follows from Fact B.3 with Xn=αnX_{n}=\alpha_{n} and the identity ηm=1/(∑k=1mαk)\eta_{m}=1/(\sum_{k=1}^{m}\alpha_{k}).

Using a different approach, we can also write

Hη\displaystyle H_{\eta} ≤∑m=1Nαm​∑n=mm+νmηn≤(∑m=1Nαm)​max⁡∑m=nn+νnn∈[N]⁡ηm=max⁡∑m=nn+νnn∈[N]⁡ηmηN.\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{N}\alpha_{m}\textstyle\sum_{n=m}^{m+\nu_{m}}\eta_{n}\leq\left(\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{N}\alpha_{m}\right)\,\max_{n\in[N]}{\textstyle\sum_{m=n}^{n+\nu_{n}}\eta_{m}}=\tfrac{\max_{n\in[N]}{\sum_{m=n}^{n+\nu_{n}}\eta_{m}}}{\eta_{N}}.

This concludes the proof. ∎

D.3 Proofs of Theorem 4.1 and Lemma 4.2

Theorem 4.1 (Restated).

Predictions {zn}n=1N\{z_{n}\}_{n=1}^{N} generated by either P-FTRL (4) or OMD (5) satisfy

ℜN​(u)≤∑n=1N1/ηn−1/ηn−12​‖zn−u‖2+12​∑n=1Nηn​‖cn‖⋆2and𝔇N≤∑n=1Nηn​νn​‖cn‖⋆.\displaystyle\mathfrak{R}_{N}(u)\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\tfrac{1/\eta_{n}-1/\eta_{n-1}}{2}\left\|z_{n}-u\right\|^{2}+\frac{1}{2}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\eta_{n}\|c_{n}\|_{\star}^{2}\quad\text{and}\quad\mathfrak{D}_{N}\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\eta_{n}\nu_{n}\|c_{n}\|_{\star}.
Proof.

The regret bound for P-FTRL follows from Theorem D.1 with regularizer functions ψn​(z)=∑m=1n1/ηm−1/ηm−12​‖zm−z‖2\psi_{n}(z)=\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{n}\tfrac{1/\eta_{m}-1/\eta_{m-1}}{2}\left\|z_{m}-z\right\|^{2}. The regret bound for OMD follows from Theorem D.4 with ψ⁡(z)=12​‖z‖2\psi(z)=\tfrac{1}{2}\|z\|^{2} so that Bψ​(x,z)=12​‖x−z‖2B_{\psi}(x;z)=\tfrac{1}{2}\|x-z\|^{2}.

For both algorithms, it holds that ‖zn+1−zn‖≤ηn​‖cn‖⋆\|z_{n+1}-z_{n}\|\leq\eta_{n}\|c_{n}\|_{\star} for all n∈[N−1]n\in[N-1], as shown in Theorem D.1 and Lemma D.5. Using triangle inequality and the fact that νm=|{n:n−λn≤m<n}|\nu_{m}=|\{n:n-\lambda_{n}\leq m<n\}|, we can write

𝔇N\displaystyle\mathfrak{D}_{N} =∑n=1N‖zn−zn−λn‖\displaystyle=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\|z_{n}-z_{n-\lambda_{n}}\|
≤∑n=1N∑m=1N𝕀(n−λn≤m<n)​‖zm+1−zm‖\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{N}\ind(n-\lambda_{n}\leq m<n)\|z_{m+1}-z_{m}\|
=∑m=1N(∑n=1N𝕀(n−λn≤m<n))​‖zm+1−zm‖\displaystyle=\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{N}(\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\ind(n-\lambda_{n}\leq m<n))\|z_{m+1}-z_{m}\|
=∑m=1Nνm​‖zm+1−zm‖\displaystyle=\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{N}\nu_{m}\|z_{m+1}-z_{m}\|
≤∑m=1Nηm​νm​‖cm‖⋆,\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{N}\eta_{m}\nu_{m}\|c_{m}\|_{\star},

where the final inequality plugs-in ‖zm+1−zm‖≤ηm​‖cm‖⋆\|z_{m+1}-z_{m}\|\leq\eta_{m}\|c_{m}\|_{\star} for single-step drifts. ∎

Lemma 4.2 (Restated).

Predictions {zn}n=1N\{z_{n}\}_{n=1}^{N} generated by P-FTRL (4) satisfy

𝔇N≤∑n=1Nηn​‖∑m=n−λnn−1cm‖⋆+D​HηwhereHη=∑n=1N(1−ηn/ηn−λn).\displaystyle\mathfrak{D}_{N}\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\eta_{n}\|\textstyle\sum_{m=n-\lambda_{n}}^{n-1}c_{m}\|_{\star}+D\,H_{\eta}\quad\text{where}\quad H_{\eta}=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}(1-\eta_{n}/\eta_{n-\lambda_{n}}).
Proof.

From Lemma D.5, we write

𝔇N\displaystyle\mathfrak{D}_{N} =∑n=1N‖zn−zn−λn‖\displaystyle=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\|z_{n}-z_{n-\lambda_{n}}\|
≤∑n=1N(ηn​‖∑m=n−λnn−1cm‖⋆+(1−ηn/ηn−λn)​D)\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\left(\eta_{n}\,\|\textstyle\sum_{m=n-\lambda_{n}}^{n-1}c_{m}\|_{\star}+(1-\eta_{n}/\eta_{n-\lambda_{n}})D\right)
=∑n=1Nηn​‖∑m=n−λnn−1cm‖⋆+D​Hη.∎\displaystyle=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{N}\eta_{n}\,\|\textstyle\sum_{m=n-\lambda_{n}}^{n-1}c_{m}\|_{\star}+DH_{\eta}.\qed

Appendix E Guarantees for OCO and BCO with Delays: Proofs

E.1 Proof of Theorem 5.2

Theorem 5.2 (Restated).

For any base algorithm ℬ\mathcal{B} and comparator u∈𝒦u\in\mathcal{K}, 𝒲OCO​(ℬ)\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{OCO}}(\mathcal{B}) guarantees

RT​(u)≤ℜTdrift​(u,G),\displaystyle R_{T}(u)\leq\mathfrak{R}^{\textnormal{drift}}_{T}(u;G),

where ℜTdrift​(u,W)\mathfrak{R}^{\textnormal{drift}}_{T}(u;W) is the drift-penalized regret of ℬ\mathcal{B} with loss vectors cn=g~nc_{n}=\widetilde{g}_{n} and lags λn=d~n⋆\lambda_{n}=\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}.

Under λ\lambda-strong convexity (2.3), it further holds that

RT​(u)≤ℜTdrift​(u,3​G)−λ2​∑n=1T‖zn−u‖2.\displaystyle R_{T}(u)\leq\mathfrak{R}^{\textnormal{drift}}_{T}(u;3G)-\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\|z_{n}\!-\!u\|^{2}.
Proof.

The drift-penalized regret of ℬ\mathcal{B} for these loss vectors and lags is defined as

ℜTdrift​(u,W)=∑n=1T⟨g~n,zn−u⟩+W​∑n=1T‖zn−d~n⋆−zn‖.\displaystyle\mathfrak{R}^{\textnormal{drift}}_{T}(u;W)=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\langle{\widetilde{g}_{n},\,z_{n}-u}\rangle+W\,\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-z_{n}\|.

We treat the general convex case as 00-strongly convex. For λ≥0\lambda\geq 0, the λ\lambda-strong convexity of the loss functions ftf_{t} gives

∑t=1T(ft​(xt)−ft​(u))\displaystyle\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}(f_{t}(x_{t})-f_{t}(u)) ≤∑t=1T⟨gt,xt−u⟩−λ2​∑t=1T‖xt−u‖2\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\langle{g_{t},\,x_{t}-u}\rangle-\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left\|x_{t}-u\right\|^{2}
=(a)∑n=1T⟨g~n,x~n−u⟩−λ2​∑n=1T‖x~n−u‖2\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{(a)}}}{{=}}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\langle{\widetilde{g}_{n},\,\widetilde{x}_{n}-u}\rangle-\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\left\|\widetilde{x}_{n}-u\right\|^{2}
=(b)∑n=1T⟨g~n,zn−d~n⋆−u⟩−λ2​∑n=1T‖zn−d~n⋆−u‖2\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{(b)}}}{{=}}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\langle{\widetilde{g}_{n},\,z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-u}\rangle-\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-u\|^{2}
≤∑n=1T⟨g~n,zn−u⟩+∑n=1T‖g~n‖⋆​‖zn−d~n⋆−zn‖−λ2​∑n=1T‖zn−d~n⋆−u‖2\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\langle{\widetilde{g}_{n},\,z_{n}-u}\rangle+\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\|\widetilde{g}_{n}\|_{\star}\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-z_{n}\|-\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-u\|^{2}
≤(c)∑n=1T⟨g~n,zn−u⟩+G​∑n=1T‖zn−d~n⋆−zn‖−λ2​∑n=1T‖zn−d~n⋆−u‖2,\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{(c)}}}{{\leq}}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\langle{\widetilde{g}_{n},\,z_{n}-u}\rangle+G\,\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-z_{n}\|-\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-u\|^{2},

where (a) replaces sequences {xt}t=1T\{x_{t}\}_{t=1}^{T}, {gt}t=1T\{g_{t}\}_{t=1}^{T} with their observation-orderings (Definition 3.5), (b) substitutes x~n=zn−d~n⋆\widetilde{x}_{n}=z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}} which follows from Lemma 3.6, and (c) applies the gradient norm bound (Assumption 2.2).

For the general convex case (λ=0\lambda=0), this immediately gives RT​(u)≤ℜTdrift​(u,G)R_{T}(u)\leq\mathfrak{R}^{\textnormal{drift}}_{T}(u;G).

For the strongly convex case (λ>0\lambda>0), we convert the distance terms from zn−d~n⋆z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}} to znz_{n}. Since ‖zn−d~n⋆−u‖,‖zn−u‖≤2​Gλ\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-u\|,\|z_{n}-u\|\leq\frac{2G}{\lambda} by Fact B.1, we have

λ2​(‖zn−u‖2−‖zn−d~n⋆−u‖2)=λ2​⟨zn−d~n⋆+zn−2​u,zn−zn−d~n⋆⟩≤2​G​‖zn−d~n⋆−zn‖.\displaystyle\tfrac{\lambda}{2}(\|z_{n}-u\|^{2}-\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-u\|^{2})=\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\,\langle{z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}+z_{n}-2u,\,z_{n}-z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}}\rangle\leq 2G\,\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-z_{n}\|.

Summing over nn and rearranging yields RT​(u)≤ℜTdrift​(u,3​G)−λ2​∑n=1T‖zn−u‖2R_{T}(u)\leq\mathfrak{R}^{\textnormal{drift}}_{T}(u;3G)-\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\|z_{n}-u\|^{2}. ∎

E.2 Proofs of Corollaries 5.3 and 5.4

Theorem E.1.

𝒲OCO​(ℬ)\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{OCO}}(\mathcal{B}), where ℬ\mathcal{B} executes P-FTRL (4) updates, guarantees that in the

general convex case:\displaystyle\text{general convex case}\colon RT​(u)≤D22​ηT+G2​∑n=1Tηn​(σ~n⋆+1),\displaystyle\,R_{T}(u)\leq\tfrac{D^{2}}{2\eta_{T}}+G^{2}\,\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\,(\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}+1),
strongly convex case (2.3):\displaystyle\text{strongly convex case (\ref{assump:strong-convexity})}\colon RT​(u)≤∑n=1T1/ηn−1/ηn−1−λ2​‖zn−u‖2+3​G2​∑n=1Tηn​(d~n⋆+1)+3​G​D​Hη,\displaystyle\,R_{T}(u)\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\tfrac{1/\eta_{n}-1/\eta_{n-1}-\lambda}{2}\left\|z_{n}\!-\!u\right\|^{2}+3G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}(\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}\!+\!1)+3GDH_{\eta},

where Hη=∑n=1T(1−ηn/ηn−d~n⋆)H_{\eta}=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}(1-\eta_{n}/{\eta_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}}) denotes the total learning rate misalignment.

Proof.

Both results follow from Theorem 5.2 once we bound the standard regret ℜT​(u)=∑n=1T⟨g~n,zn−u⟩\mathfrak{R}_{T}(u)=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\langle{\widetilde{g}_{n},\,z_{n}-u}\rangle and prediction drift 𝔇T=∑n=1T‖zn−d~n⋆−zn‖\mathfrak{D}_{T}=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-z_{n}\| components.

To control ℜT​(u)\mathfrak{R}_{T}(u) in both cases, apply Theorem 4.1 for ‖g~n‖⋆≤G\|\widetilde{g}_{n}\|_{\star}\leq G and ‖zn−u‖≤D\|z_{n}-u\|\leq D, as follows

ℜT​(u)\displaystyle\mathfrak{R}_{T}(u) ≤∑n=1T1/ηn−1/ηn−12​‖zm−u‖2+12​∑n=1Tηn​‖gn‖⋆2≤D22​ηT+G2​∑n=1Tηn.\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\tfrac{1/\eta_{n}-1/\eta_{n-1}}{2}\left\|z_{m}-u\right\|^{2}+\frac{1}{2}\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\|g_{n}\|_{\star}^{2}\leq\tfrac{D^{2}}{2\eta_{T}}+G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}.

To control 𝔇T\mathfrak{D}_{T} in the general convex case, use Theorem 4.1 to write

𝔇T\displaystyle\mathfrak{D}_{T} ≤∑n=1Tηn​σ~n⋆​‖g~n‖⋆≤G​∑n=1Tηn​σ~n⋆.\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}\|\widetilde{g}_{n}\|_{\star}\leq G\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}.

Then, the general convex case follows from the corresponding inequality in Theorem 5.2:

RT​(u)≤ℜT​(u)+G​𝔇T≤D22​ηT+G2​∑n=1Tηn+G2​∑n=1Tηn​σ~n⋆≤D22​ηT+G2​∑n=1Tηn​(σ~n⋆+1).\displaystyle R_{T}(u)\leq\mathfrak{R}_{T}(u)+G\,\mathfrak{D}_{T}\leq\tfrac{D^{2}}{2\eta_{T}}+G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}+G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\,\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}\leq\tfrac{D^{2}}{2\eta_{T}}+G^{2}\,\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\,(\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}+1).

To control 𝔇T\mathfrak{D}_{T} in the strongly convex case, use Lemma 4.2 to write

𝔇T≤∑n=1Tηn​‖∑m=n−d~n⋆n−1g~m‖⋆+D​Hη≤G​∑n=1Tηn​d~n⋆+D​Hη,\displaystyle\mathfrak{D}_{T}\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\|\textstyle\sum_{m=n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}^{n-1}\widetilde{g}_{m}\|_{\star}+D\,H_{\eta}\leq G\,\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+D\,H_{\eta},

where Hη=∑n=1T(1−ηn/ηn−d~n⋆)H_{\eta}=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}(1-\eta_{n}/{\eta_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}}) in this case with lags λn=d~n⋆\lambda_{n}=\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}.

Finally, the strongly convex case follows from the corresponding inequality in Theorem 5.2:

RT​(u)\displaystyle R_{T}(u) ≤ℜT​(u)−λ2​∑n=1T‖zn−u‖2+3​G​𝔇T\displaystyle\leq\mathfrak{R}_{T}(u)-\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\|z_{n}-u\|^{2}+3G\,\mathfrak{D}_{T}
≤∑n=1T1/ηn−1/ηn−1−λ2​‖zn−u‖2+G2​∑n=1Tηn+3​G2​∑n=1Tηn​d~n⋆+3​G​D​Hη\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\tfrac{1/\eta_{n}-1/\eta_{n-1}-\lambda}{2}\left\|z_{n}\!-\!u\right\|^{2}+G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}+3G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+3GDH_{\eta}
≤∑n=1T1/ηn−1/ηn−1−λ2​‖zn−u‖2+3​G2​∑n=1Tηn​(d~n⋆+1)+3​G​D​Hη.\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\tfrac{1/\eta_{n}-1/\eta_{n-1}-\lambda}{2}\left\|z_{n}\!-\!u\right\|^{2}+3G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}(\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}\!+\!1)+3GDH_{\eta}.

This concludes the proof for both cases. ∎

Theorem E.2.

𝒲OCO​(ℬ)\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{OCO}}(\mathcal{B}), where ℬ\mathcal{B} executes OMD (5) updates, guarantees that in the

general convex convex:\displaystyle\text{general convex convex}\colon RT​(u)≤D22​ηT+G2​∑n=1Tηn​(σ~n⋆+1),\displaystyle\,\,R_{T}(u)\leq\tfrac{D^{2}}{2\eta_{T}}+G^{2}\,\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\,(\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}+1),
strongly convex case (2.3):\displaystyle\text{strongly convex case (\ref{assump:strong-convexity})}\colon RT​(u)≤∑n=1T1/ηn−1/ηn−1−λ2​‖zn−u‖2+3​G2​∑n=1Tηn​(σ~n⋆+1).\displaystyle\,\,R_{T}(u)\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\tfrac{1/\eta_{n}-1/\eta_{n-1}-\lambda}{2}\left\|z_{n}-u\right\|^{2}+3G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}(\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}+1).
Proof.

As in the proof of Theorem E.1, we use Theorem 4.1 to show that

ℜT​(u)≤∑n=1T1/ηn−1/ηn−12​‖zm−u‖2+G2​∑n=1Tηnand𝔇T≤G​∑n=1Tηn​σ~n⋆.\displaystyle\mathfrak{R}_{T}(u)\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\tfrac{1/\eta_{n}-1/\eta_{n-1}}{2}\left\|z_{m}-u\right\|^{2}+G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\quad\text{and}\quad\mathfrak{D}_{T}\leq G\,\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\,\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}.

The general convex case similarly follows from its corresponding inequality in Theorem 5.2:

RT​(u)≤ℜT​(u)+G​𝔇T≤D22​ηT+G2​∑n=1Tηn+G2​∑n=1Tηn​σ~n⋆≤D22​ηT+G2​∑n=1Tηn​(σ~n⋆+1).\displaystyle R_{T}(u)\leq\mathfrak{R}_{T}(u)+G\,\mathfrak{D}_{T}\leq\tfrac{D^{2}}{2\eta_{T}}+G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}+G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\,\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}\leq\tfrac{D^{2}}{2\eta_{T}}+G^{2}\,\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\,(\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}+1).

The strongly convex case also follows from its corresponding inequality in Theorem 5.2:

RT​(u)\displaystyle R_{T}(u) ≤ℜT​(u)−λ2​∑n=1T‖zn−u‖2+3​G​𝔇T\displaystyle\leq\mathfrak{R}_{T}(u)-\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\|z_{n}-u\|^{2}+3G\,\mathfrak{D}_{T}
≤∑n=1T1/ηn−1/ηn−1−λ2​‖zn−u‖2+G2​∑n=1Tηn+3​G2​∑n=1Tηn​σ~n⋆\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\tfrac{1/\eta_{n}-1/\eta_{n-1}-\lambda}{2}\left\|z_{n}\!-\!u\right\|^{2}+G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}+3G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}
≤∑n=1T1/ηn−1/ηn−1−λ2​‖zn−u‖2+3​G2​∑n=1Tηn​(σ~n⋆+1).\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\tfrac{1/\eta_{n}-1/\eta_{n-1}-\lambda}{2}\left\|z_{n}\!-\!u\right\|^{2}+3G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}(\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}+1).

This concludes the proof for both cases. ∎

Corollary 5.3 (Restated).

𝒲OCO​(ℬ)\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{OCO}}(\mathcal{B}), where ℬ\mathcal{B} runs P-FTRL (4) or OMD (5) with ηn=D/Gn+∑m=1nσ~m⋆\eta_{n}=\frac{D/G}{\sqrt{n+\sum_{m=1}^{n}\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{m}}}, guarantees

RT​(x∗)=O⁡(G​D​[dtot+T]).\displaystyle R_{T}(x^{*})=O\left(GD\,\left[\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}}+\sqrt{T}\right]\right).
Proof.

Using the general convex case of Theorem E.1 for P-FTRL and Theorem E.2 for OMD, we can write

RT​(x∗)\displaystyle R_{T}(x^{*}) ≤D22​ηT+G2​∑n=1Tηn​(σ~n⋆+1)\displaystyle\leq\tfrac{D^{2}}{2\eta_{T}}+G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}(\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}+1)
≤(a)G​D​T+∑n=1Tσ~n⋆+2​G​D​∑n=1T(σ~n⋆+1)\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{(a)}}}{{\leq}}GD\,\sqrt{T+\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}}+2GD\,\sqrt{\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}(\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}+1)}
=(b)3​G​D​T+dtot\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{(b)}}}{{=}}3GD\,\sqrt{T+d_{\textnormal{tot}}}
≤6​G​D​[dtot+T],\displaystyle\leq 6GD\left[\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}}+\sqrt{T}\right],

where (a) substitutes learning rate values and applies Fact B.4 for Xn=σ~n⋆+1X_{n}=\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}+1 and (b) uses the indentity ∑t=1Tσt⋆=dtot\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sigma^{\star}_{t}=d_{\textnormal{tot}} from Theorem 3.4. ∎

Corollary 5.4 (Restated).

Under λ\lambda-strong convexity (2.3), 𝒲OCO​(ℬ)\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{OCO}}(\mathcal{B}), where ℬ\mathcal{B} runs P-FTRL (4) with ηn=1n​λ\eta_{n}=\tfrac{1}{n\lambda}, guarantees

RT​(x∗)=O⁡(G2λ​[min⁡{σmax​ln⁡T,dtot}+ln⁡T]).\displaystyle R_{T}(x^{*})=O\left(\tfrac{G^{2}}{\lambda}\left[\min\left\{\sigma_{\textnormal{max}}\ln T,\,\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}}\right\}+\ln T\right]\right).

Running OMD (5) with ηn=1n​λ\eta_{n}=\frac{1}{n\lambda} instead guarantees

RT​(x∗)=O⁡(G2λ​(σmax+1)​ln⁡T).\displaystyle R_{T}(x^{*})=O\left(\tfrac{G^{2}}{\lambda}(\sigma_{\textnormal{max}}\!+\!1)\ln T\right).
Proof.

We prove the result for P-FTRL first. For learning rates ηn=1n​λ\eta_{n}=\tfrac{1}{n\lambda}, by letting D≤2​GλD\leq\frac{2G}{\lambda} (see Fact B.1), term Hη=∑n=1Tηn​(1/ηn−1/ηn−d~n⋆)H_{\eta}=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}(1/\eta_{n}-1/{\eta_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}}) can be bounded from above as

Hη=∑n=1Tηn​(λ​n−λ⁡(n−d~n⋆))=λ​∑n=1Tηn​d~n⋆≤(2​G/D)​∑n=1Tηn​d~n⋆.\displaystyle H_{\eta}=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}(\lambda n-\lambda(n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}))=\lambda\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}\leq(2G/D)\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}.

Then, using the strongly convex case of Theorem E.1, we write

RT​(x∗)\displaystyle R_{T}(x^{*}) ≤∑n=1T1/ηn−1/ηn−1−λ2​‖zn−x∗‖2+3​G2​∑n=1Tηn​(d~n⋆+1)+3​G​D​Hη\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\tfrac{1/\eta_{n}-1/\eta_{n-1}-\lambda}{2}\left\|z_{n}\!-\!x^{*}\right\|^{2}+3G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}(\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}\!+\!1)+3GDH_{\eta}
≤(a)0+3​G2​∑n=1Tηn​(d~n⋆+1)+6​G2​∑n=1Tηn​d~n⋆\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{(a)}}}{{\leq}}0+3G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}(\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}\!+\!1)+6G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}
≤(b)9​G2​∑n=1Td~n⋆+1λ​n\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{(b)}}}{{\leq}}9G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\tfrac{\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+1}{\lambda n}
≤(c)9​G2λ​(min⁡{σmax​ln⁡(e​T), 2​dtot}+ln⁡(e​T)),\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{(c)}}}{{\leq}}\tfrac{9G^{2}}{\lambda}\left(\min\{\sigma_{\textnormal{max}}\ln(eT),\,2\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}}\}+\ln(eT)\right),

where (a) substitutes learning rate values in the first term and applies the above bound on HηH_{\eta}, (b) substitutes ηn=1/(λ​n)\eta_{n}=1/(\lambda n), and (c) uses Fact C.4 for d~n⋆\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n} and Fact B.3 to get the desired bound.

For OMD, using the strongly convex case of Theorem E.2, we write

RT​(x∗)\displaystyle R_{T}(x^{*}) ≤∑n=1T1/ηn−1/ηn−1−λ2​‖zn−x∗‖2+3​G2​∑n=1Tηn​(σ~n⋆+1)\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\tfrac{1/\eta_{n}-1/\eta_{n-1}-\lambda}{2}\left\|z_{n}\!-\!x^{*}\right\|^{2}+3G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}(\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}+1)
≤(a)0+3​G2​∑n=1Tσ~n⋆+1λ​n\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{(a)}}}{{\leq}}0+3G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\tfrac{\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}+1}{\lambda n}
≤(b)3​G2λ​(σmax​ln⁡(e​T)+ln⁡(e​T)),\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{(b)}}}{{\leq}}\tfrac{3G^{2}}{\lambda}\left(\sigma_{\textnormal{max}}\ln(eT)+\ln(eT)\right),

where (a) substitutes learning rate values and (b) uses Fact C.4 for σ~n⋆\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n} to get the final bound. ∎

E.3 Proof of Theorem 5.6

In this section, we prove Theorem 5.6. We begin by recalling notation from the main body.

Algorithm ℬ\mathcal{B} generates base-predictions {zn}n=1T\{z_{n}\}_{n=1}^{T}, and in round tt the wrapper 𝒲B​C​O​(ℬ)\mathcal{W}_{BCO}(\mathcal{B}) produces prediction xt=(1−δt/r)​yt+δt​utx_{t}=(1-\delta_{t}/r)\,y_{t}+\delta_{t}u_{t}, where yt=z¯y_{t}=\widebar{z} is the current base-prediction and ut∼Unif​(𝕊k−1)u_{t}\sim\textnormal{Unif}(\mathbb{S}^{k-1}) is sampled independently. Define the shrunk suggestions ytδ=(1−δt/r)​yt∈(1−δt/r)​𝒦y^{\delta}_{t}=(1-\delta_{t}/r)\,y_{t}\in(1-\delta_{t}/r)\mathcal{K}, so that xt=ytδ+δt​utx_{t}=y^{\delta}_{t}+\delta_{t}u_{t}.

Under observation-ordering (Definition 3.5), these quantities become

y~n=zn−d~n⋆,y~nδ=(1−δ~nr)​zn−d~n⋆,x~n=y~nδ+δ~n​u~n.\displaystyle\widetilde{y}_{n}=z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}},\quad\widetilde{y}^{\delta}_{n}=(1-\tfrac{\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}{r})\,z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}},\quad\widetilde{x}_{n}=\widetilde{y}^{\delta}_{n}+\widetilde{\delta}_{n}\widetilde{u}_{n}.

For the smoothed losses f~nδ​(x)=𝔼v∼Unif​(𝔹k)​[f~n​(x+δ~n​v)]\widetilde{f}_{n}^{\delta}(x)=\mathbb{E}_{v\sim\textnormal{Unif}(\mathbb{B}^{k})}[\widetilde{f}_{n}(x+\widetilde{\delta}_{n}v)] defined on (1−δ~nr)​𝒦(1-\tfrac{\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}{r})\mathcal{K}, let g~nδ=∇f~nδ​(y~nδ)\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{n}=\nabla\widetilde{f}^{\delta}_{n}(\widetilde{y}^{\delta}_{n}).
By Theorem 5.5, the single-point estimator g^~nδ=kδ~n​f~n​(x~n)​u~n\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{n}=\tfrac{k}{\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}\widetilde{f}_{n}(\widetilde{x}_{n})\widetilde{u}_{n} satisfies 𝔼⁡[g^~nδ∣zn−d~n⋆]=g~nδ\mathbb{E}[\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{n}\mid z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}]=\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{n}.

Theorem 5.6 (Restated).

For any base-algorithm ℬ\mathcal{B}, non-increasing sequence (δt)t≥1⊂(0,r](\delta_{t})_{t\geq 1}\subset(0,r], and comparator u∈𝒦u\in\mathcal{K}, 𝒲BCO​(ℬ)\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{BCO}}(\mathcal{B}) guarantees

R¯T​(u)\displaystyle\widebar{R}_{T}(u) ≤𝔼⁡[ℜTdrift​(u,G)]+6​G​R​δtotr,\displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}\left[\mathfrak{R}^{\textnormal{drift}}_{T}(u;G)\right]+\tfrac{6GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r},

where ℜTdrift​(u,W)\mathfrak{R}^{\textnormal{drift}}_{T}(u;W) is the drift-penalized regret of ℬ\mathcal{B} on loss vectors cn=g^~nδc_{n}=\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{n} with lags λn=d~n⋆\lambda_{n}=\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}, and δtot=∑t=1Tδt\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}=\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\delta_{t}.

Under λ\lambda-strong convexity (2.3), it further holds that

R¯T​(u)\displaystyle\widebar{R}_{T}(u) ≤𝔼⁡[ℜTdrift​(u,3​G)−λ2​∑n=1T‖zn−u‖2]+10​G​R​δtotr.\displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathfrak{R}^{\textnormal{drift}}_{T}(u;3G)\!-\!\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\!\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\|z_{n}\!-\!u\|^{2}\right]\!+\!\tfrac{10GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r}.
Proof.

Fix comparator v∈𝒦v\in\mathcal{K}. For n∈[T]n\in[T], let v~nδ=(1−δ~n/r)​v\widetilde{v}^{\delta}_{n}=(1-\widetilde{\delta}_{n}/r)v which satisfies ‖v~nδ−v‖=δ~n​‖v‖r≤R​δ~nr\|\widetilde{v}^{\delta}_{n}-v\|=\tfrac{\widetilde{\delta}_{n}\left\|v\right\|}{r}\leq\tfrac{R\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}{r}. This gives

R¯T​(v)\displaystyle\widebar{R}_{T}(v) =𝔼⁡[∑n=1T(f~n​(x~n)−f~n​(v))]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\left[\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}(\widetilde{f}_{n}(\widetilde{x}_{n})-\widetilde{f}_{n}(v))\right]
=𝔼⁡[∑n=1T(f~nδ​(y~nδ)−f~nδ​(v~nδ))]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\left[\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}(\widetilde{f}^{\delta}_{n}(\widetilde{y}^{\delta}_{n})-\widetilde{f}^{\delta}_{n}(\widetilde{v}^{\delta}_{n}))\right]
+𝔼⁡[∑n=1T(f~n​(x~n)−f~n​(y~nδ))]+𝔼⁡[∑n=1T(f~n​(y~nδ)−f~nδ​(y~nδ))]\displaystyle+\mathbb{E}\left[\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}(\widetilde{f}_{n}(\widetilde{x}_{n})-\widetilde{f}_{n}(\widetilde{y}^{\delta}_{n}))\right]+\mathbb{E}\left[\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}(\widetilde{f}_{n}(\widetilde{y}^{\delta}_{n})-\widetilde{f}^{\delta}_{n}(\widetilde{y}^{\delta}_{n}))\right]
+𝔼⁡[∑n=1T(f~nδ​(v~nδ)−f~n​(v~nδ))]+𝔼⁡[∑n=1T(f~n​(v~nδ)−f~n​(v))]\displaystyle+\mathbb{E}\left[\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}(\widetilde{f}^{\delta}_{n}(\widetilde{v}^{\delta}_{n})-\widetilde{f}_{n}(\widetilde{v}^{\delta}_{n}))\right]+\mathbb{E}\left[\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}(\widetilde{f}_{n}(\widetilde{v}^{\delta}_{n})-\widetilde{f}_{n}(v))\right]
≤(a)𝔼⁡[∑n=1T(f~nδ​(y~nδ)−f~nδ​(v~nδ))]+∑n=1T(G​δ~n+G​δ~n+G​δ~n+G​Rr​δ~n)\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{(a)}}}{{\leq}}\mathbb{E}\left[\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}(\widetilde{f}^{\delta}_{n}(\widetilde{y}^{\delta}_{n})-\widetilde{f}^{\delta}_{n}(\widetilde{v}^{\delta}_{n}))\right]+\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\left(G\widetilde{\delta}_{n}+G\widetilde{\delta}_{n}+G\widetilde{\delta}_{n}+\tfrac{GR}{r}\widetilde{\delta}_{n}\right)
≤(b)𝔼⁡[∑n=1T(⟨g~nδ,y~nδ−v~nδ⟩−λ2​‖y~nδ−v~nδ‖2)]+4​G​R​δtotr\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{(b)}}}{{\leq}}\mathbb{E}\left[\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\left(\langle{\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{n},\,\widetilde{y}^{\delta}_{n}-\widetilde{v}^{\delta}_{n}}\rangle-\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\|\widetilde{y}^{\delta}_{n}-\widetilde{v}^{\delta}_{n}\|^{2}\right)\right]+\tfrac{4GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r}
=(c)𝔼⁡[∑n=1T((1−δ~nr)​⟨g~nδ,zn−d~n⋆−v⟩−λ2​(1−δ~nr)2​‖zn−d~n⋆−v‖2)]+4​G​R​δtotr\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{(c)}}}{{=}}\mathbb{E}\left[\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\left((1-\tfrac{\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}{r})\,\langle{\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{n},\,z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-v}\rangle-\tfrac{\lambda}{2}(1-\tfrac{\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}{r})^{2}\,\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-v\|^{2}\right)\right]+\tfrac{4GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r}
=𝔼⁡[∑n=1T(⟨g~nδ,zn−v⟩−λ2​‖zn−d~n⋆−v‖2+⟨g~nδ,zn−d~n⋆−zn⟩)]+4​G​R​δtotr\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\left[\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\left(\langle{\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{n},\,z_{n}-v}\rangle-\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-v\|^{2}+\langle{\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{n},\,z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-z_{n}}\rangle\right)\right]+\tfrac{4GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r}
+𝔼⁡[∑n=1T(δ~nr​⟨g~nδ,v−zn−d~n⋆⟩+(λ​δ~nr−λ​δ~n22​r2)​‖zn−d~n⋆−v‖2)].\displaystyle+\mathbb{E}\left[\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}(\tfrac{\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}{r}\langle{\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{n},\,v-z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}}\rangle+(\tfrac{\lambda\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}{r}-\tfrac{\lambda\widetilde{\delta}_{n}^{2}}{2r^{2}})\,\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-v\|^{2})\right]. (6)

where (a) uses GG-Lipschitzness of f~n\widetilde{f}_{n} and Theorem 5.5 to bound the last four terms in the previous line, (b) uses λ\lambda-strong convexity of f~nδ\widetilde{f}^{\delta}_{n}, and (c) substitutes y~nδ=(1−δ~nr)​zn−d~n⋆\widetilde{y}^{\delta}_{n}=(1-\tfrac{\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}{r})z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}} and v~nδ=(1−δ~nr)​v\widetilde{v}^{\delta}_{n}=(1-\tfrac{\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}{r})v.

The final term in (6) can be bound using Cauchy-Schwartz inequality as follows:

𝔼⁡[∑n=1T(δ~nr​⟨g~nδ,v−zn−d~n⋆⟩+(λ​δ~nr−λ​δ~n22​r2)​‖zn−d~n⋆−v‖2)]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}(\tfrac{\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}{r}\langle{\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{n},\,v-z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}}\rangle+(\tfrac{\lambda\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}{r}-\tfrac{\lambda\widetilde{\delta}_{n}^{2}}{2r^{2}})\,\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-v\|^{2})\right]
≤𝔼⁡[∑n=1T(δ~nr​‖g~nδ‖⋆​‖zn−d~n⋆−v‖+λ​δ~nr​‖zn−d~n⋆−v‖2)]\displaystyle\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\leq\mathbb{E}\left[\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}(\tfrac{\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}{r}\|\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{n}\|_{\star}\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-v\|+\tfrac{\lambda\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}{r}\,\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-v\|^{2})\right]
≤(d)∑n=1T(G​D​δ~nr+λ​D2​δ~nr)=(G+λ​D)​D​δtotr,\displaystyle\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{(d)}}}{{\leq}}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\left(\tfrac{GD\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}{r}+\tfrac{\lambda D^{2}\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}{r}\right)=\tfrac{(G+\lambda D)D\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r}, (7)

where (d) follows from the facts that ‖zn−d~n⋆−v‖≤D\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-v\|\leq D and ‖g~nδ‖⋆≤G\|\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{n}\|_{\star}\leq G due to Theorem 5.5.

For every n∈[T]n\in[T], the direction u~n\widetilde{u}_{n} and base-prediction znz_{n} are independent: u~n\widetilde{u}_{n} is sampled when making the nn-th prediction and only affects the nn-th observation f~n​(x~n)=f~n​((1−δ~n/r)​zn−d~n⋆+δ~n​u~n)\widetilde{f}_{n}(\widetilde{x}_{n})=\widetilde{f}_{n}((1-\widetilde{\delta}_{n}/r)\,z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}+\widetilde{\delta}_{n}\widetilde{u}_{n}), whereas znz_{n} is the output of ℬ\mathcal{B} after processing the (n−1)(n-1)-th observation. By Theorem 5.5,

𝔼⁡[g^~nδ∣zn]=𝔼⁡[kδ~n​f~n​(x~n)​u~n∣zn]=∇f~nδ​((1−δ~nr)​zn−d~n⋆)=g~nδ.\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{n}\mid z_{n}]=\mathbb{E}\left[\tfrac{k}{\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}\widetilde{f}_{n}(\widetilde{x}_{n})\widetilde{u}_{n}\mid z_{n}\right]=\nabla\widetilde{f}^{\delta}_{n}\left((1-\tfrac{\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}{r})\,z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}\right)=\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{n}.

Hence, the expected regret term 𝔼⁡[ℜ⁡(u)]\mathbb{E}[\mathfrak{R}(u)] satisfies

𝔼⁡[ℜ⁡(u)]=𝔼⁡[∑n=1T⟨g^~nδ,zn−u⟩]=(e)𝔼⁡[∑n=1T⟨g~nδ,zn−u⟩].\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\mathfrak{R}(u)\right]=\mathbb{E}\left[\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\langle{\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{n},\,z_{n}-u}\rangle\right]\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{(e)}}}{{=}}\mathbb{E}\left[\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\langle{\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{n},\,z_{n}-u}\rangle\right]. (8)

Combining (6), (7), (8) and the facts that D≤2​RD\leq 2R and ⟨g~nδ,zn−d~n⋆−zn⟩≤G​‖zn−d~n⋆−zn‖\langle{\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{n},\,z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-z_{n}}\rangle\leq G\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-z_{n}\|, we have

R¯T​(v)≤𝔼⁡[ℜT​(v)−λ2​∑n=1T‖zn−d~n⋆−v‖2+G​𝔇T]+(6​G+2​λ​D)​R​δtotr.\displaystyle\widebar{R}_{T}(v)\leq\mathbb{E}\left[\mathfrak{R}_{T}(v)-\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-v\|^{2}+G\mathfrak{D}_{T}\right]+\tfrac{(6G+2\lambda D)R\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r}. (9)

This concludes the proof for the convex case (λ=0\lambda=0). It remains to consider the strongly convex case (λ>0\lambda>0).

For all n∈[T]n\in[T],

λ2​(‖zn−u‖2−‖zn−d~n⋆−u‖2)\displaystyle\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\left(\|z_{n}-u\|^{2}-\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-u\|^{2}\right) =λ2​⟨zn−d~n⋆+zn−2​u,zn−zn−d~n⋆⟩≤λ​D​‖zn−d~n⋆−zn‖.\displaystyle=\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\langle{z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}+z_{n}-2u,\,z_{n}-z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}}\rangle\leq\lambda D\,\|z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}-z_{n}\|.

Combining with (9) and letting D≤2​GλD\leq\frac{2G}{\lambda} (see Fact B.1) yields

R¯T​(u)≤𝔼⁡[ℜT​(u)−λ2​∑n=1T‖zn−u‖2+3​G​𝔇T]+10​G​R​δtotr.\displaystyle\widebar{R}_{T}(u)\leq\mathbb{E}\left[\mathfrak{R}_{T}(u)-\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\|z_{n}-u\|^{2}+3G\,\mathfrak{D}_{T}\right]+\tfrac{10GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r}.

This completes the proof. ∎

E.4 Proofs of Corollaries 5.7 and 5.8

Theorem E.3.

𝒲BCO​(ℬ)\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{BCO}}(\mathcal{B}), where ℬ\mathcal{B} executes P-FTRL (4) updates, guarantees that in the

general convex convex:R¯T​(u)\displaystyle\text{general convex convex}\colon\,\widebar{R}_{T}(u) ≤D22​ηT+∑n=1Tηn​(G​𝔼​[‖Γn‖]+(k​M/δ~n)2)+G​D​Hη+6​G​R​δtotr,\displaystyle\leq\tfrac{D^{2}}{2\eta_{T}}+\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\left(G\,\mathbb{E}[\|\Gamma_{n}\|]+({kM}/{\widetilde{\delta}_{n}})^{2}\right)+GDH_{\eta}+\tfrac{6GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r},
strongly convex case (2.3):R¯T​(u)\displaystyle\text{strongly convex case (\ref{assump:strong-convexity})}\colon\,\widebar{R}_{T}(u) ≤∑n=1T1/ηn−1/ηn−1−λ2​𝔼​[‖zn−u‖2]\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\tfrac{1/\eta_{n}-1/\eta_{n-1}-\lambda}{2}\,\mathbb{E}[\left\|z_{n}\!-\!u\right\|^{2}]
+∑n=1Tηn(3G𝔼[∥Γn∥]+(kM/δ~n)2)+3GDHη+10​G​R​δtotr,\displaystyle+\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\left(3G\,\mathbb{E}[\|\Gamma_{n}\|]+({kM}/{\widetilde{\delta}_{n}})^{2}\right)+3GDH_{\eta}+\tfrac{10GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r},

where Γn=∑m=n−d~n⋆n−1g^~mδ\Gamma_{n}=\textstyle\sum_{m=n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}^{n-1}\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{m} and Hη=∑n=1T(1−ηn/ηn−d~n⋆)H_{\eta}=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}(1-\eta_{n}/{\eta_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}}).

Proof.

Both results follow from Theorem 5.6 once we bound ℜT​(u)\mathfrak{R}_{T}(u) and 𝔇T\mathfrak{D}_{T} components of ℜTdrift​(u,W)\mathfrak{R}^{\textnormal{drift}}_{T}(u;W).

To control ℜT​(u)\mathfrak{R}_{T}(u) in both cases, apply Theorem 4.1 for ‖g^~nδ‖≤k​M/δ~n\|\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{n}\|\leq kM/\widetilde{\delta}_{n} and ‖zn−u‖≤D\|z_{n}-u\|\leq D, as follows

ℜT​(u)≤∑n=1T1/ηn−1/ηn−12​‖zm−u‖2+12​∑n=1Tηn​‖g^~nδ‖2≤D22​ηT+∑n=1Tηn​(k​M/δ~n)2.\displaystyle\mathfrak{R}_{T}(u)\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\tfrac{1/\eta_{n}-1/\eta_{n-1}}{2}\left\|z_{m}-u\right\|^{2}+\frac{1}{2}\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\|\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{n}\|^{2}\leq\tfrac{D^{2}}{2\eta_{T}}+\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}(kM/\widetilde{\delta}_{n})^{2}.

To control 𝔇T=∑n=1T‖zn−zn−d~n⋆‖\mathfrak{D}_{T}=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\|z_{n}\!-\!z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}\|, we use Lemma 4.2 to write

𝔇T≤∑n=1Tηn​(‖∑m=n−d~n⋆n−1g^~mδ‖⋆+(1/ηn−1/ηn−d~n⋆)​D)≤∑n=1Tηn​‖Γn‖+D​Hη.\displaystyle\mathfrak{D}_{T}\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\left(\|\textstyle\sum_{m=n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}^{n-1}\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{m}\|_{\star}+(1/\eta_{n}-1/\eta_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}})D\right)\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\|\Gamma_{n}\|+DH_{\eta}.

Then, the general convex case follows from the corresponding inequality in Theorem 5.6, as follows:

R¯T​(u)\displaystyle\widebar{R}_{T}(u) ≤𝔼⁡[ℜT​(u)+G​𝔇T]+6​G​R​δtotr\displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}\left[\mathfrak{R}_{T}(u)+G\,\mathfrak{D}_{T}\right]+\tfrac{6GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r}
≤D22​ηT+∑n=1Tηn​(k​M/δ~n)2+G​∑n=1Tηn​𝔼​[‖Γn‖]+G​D​Hη+6​G​R​δtotr\displaystyle\leq\tfrac{D^{2}}{2\eta_{T}}+\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}(kM/\widetilde{\delta}_{n})^{2}+G\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\mathbb{E}[\|\Gamma_{n}\|]+GDH_{\eta}+\tfrac{6GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r}
=D22​ηT+∑n=1Tηn​(G​𝔼​[‖Γn‖]+(k​M/δ~n)2)+G​D​Hη+6​G​R​δtotr.\displaystyle=\tfrac{D^{2}}{2\eta_{T}}+\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\left(G\,\mathbb{E}[\|\Gamma_{n}\|]+({kM}/{\widetilde{\delta}_{n}})^{2}\right)+GDH_{\eta}+\tfrac{6GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r}.

The strongly convex case follows from the corresponding inequality in Theorem 5.6:

R¯T​(u)\displaystyle\widebar{R}_{T}(u) ≤𝔼⁡[ℜT​(u)−λ2​∑n=1T‖zn−u‖2+3​G​𝔇T]+10​G​R​δtotr\displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}\left[\mathfrak{R}_{T}(u)-\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\|z_{n}-u\|^{2}+3G\mathfrak{D}_{T}\right]+\tfrac{10GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r}
≤∑n=1T1/ηn−1/ηn−1−λ2​𝔼​[‖zn−u‖2]+∑n=1Tηn​(k​Mδ~n)2+3​G​(∑n=1Tηn​𝔼​[‖Γn‖]+D​Hη)+10​G​R​δtotr\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\tfrac{1/\eta_{n}-1/\eta_{n-1}-\lambda}{2}\mathbb{E}[\left\|z_{n}\!-\!u\right\|^{2}]\!+\!\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}(\tfrac{kM}{\widetilde{\delta}_{n}})^{2}\!+\!3G\left(\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\mathbb{E}[\|\Gamma_{n}\|]\!+\!DH_{\eta}\right)\!+\!\tfrac{10GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r}
=∑n=1T1/ηn−1/ηn−1−λ2​𝔼​[‖zn−u‖2]+∑n=1Tηn​(3​G​𝔼​[‖Γn‖]+(k​M/δ~n)2)+3​G​D​Hη+10​G​R​δtotr.\displaystyle=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\tfrac{1/\eta_{n}-1/\eta_{n-1}-\lambda}{2}\,\mathbb{E}[\left\|z_{n}\!-\!u\right\|^{2}]+\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\left(3G\,\mathbb{E}[\|\Gamma_{n}\|]\!+\!({kM}/{\widetilde{\delta}_{n}})^{2}\right)\!+\!3GDH_{\eta}\!+\!\tfrac{10GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r}.

This concludes the proof for both cases. ∎

Lemma E.4.

For Γn=∑m=n−d~n⋆n−1g^~mδ\Gamma_{n}=\textstyle\sum_{m=n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}^{n-1}\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{m} from Theorem E.3 and δn′=δρ⁡(n)+dρ⁡(n)\delta^{\prime}_{n}=\delta_{\rho(n)+d_{\rho(n)}}, it holds that

G​𝔼​[‖Γn‖]≤4​(G2​d~n⋆+(k​M/δn′)2).\displaystyle G\,\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\Gamma_{n}\right\|\right]\leq 4(G^{2}\,\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+({kM}/{\delta^{\prime}_{n}})^{2}).
Proof.

Note that ‖g~nδ‖≤G\|\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{n}\|\leq G and ‖g^~nδ‖≤k​Mδ~n\|\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{n}\|\leq\frac{kM}{\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}. With probability one, it holds that

‖Γn‖≤∑m=n−d~n⋆n−1∥g~mδ∥+∥∑m=n−d~n⋆n−1(g^~mδ−g~mδ)⏟=:Mn∥≤Gd~n⋆+∥Mn∥.\displaystyle\left\|\Gamma_{n}\right\|\leq\textstyle\sum_{m=n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}^{n-1}\|\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{m}\|+\|\underbrace{\textstyle\sum_{m=n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}^{n-1}(\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{m}-\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{m})}_{=:M_{n}}\|\leq G\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+\|M_{n}\|.

Since δn′=δρ⁡(n)+dρ⁡(n)\delta^{\prime}_{n}=\delta_{\rho(n)+d_{\rho(n)}}, it holds that δn′≤δt\delta^{\prime}_{n}\leq\delta_{t} for all t∈{s:rs∈Iρ⁡(n)}t\in\{s:r_{s}\in I_{\rho(n)}\}, because for all such tt we have lt<rt<rρ⁡(n)<lρ⁡(n)+dρ⁡(n)+1l_{t}<r_{t}<r_{\rho(n)}<l_{\rho(n)+d_{\rho(n)}+1} (i.e., t≤ρ⁡(n)+dρ⁡(n)t\leq\rho(n)+d_{\rho(n)}) and sequence (δt)t=1T(\delta_{t})_{t=1}^{T} is non-increasing.

Let G′=G+k​M/δn′G^{\prime}=G+kM/\delta^{\prime}_{n} so that ‖g^tδ−gtδ‖≤G′\|\widehat{g}^{\delta}_{t}-g^{\delta}_{t}\|\leq G^{\prime} for all t∈{s:rs∈Iρ⁡(n)}t\in\{s:r_{s}\in I_{\rho(n)}\}.

Let vt=(g^tδ−gtδ)𝕀(rt∈Iρ⁡(n))v_{t}=(\widehat{g}^{\delta}_{t}-g^{\delta}_{t})\ind(r_{t}\in I_{\rho(n)}) for t∈[T]t\in[T], so that Mn=∑t=1TvtM_{n}=\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}v_{t}, 𝔼⁡[vt]=0\mathbb{E}[v_{t}]=0, and ∥vt∥≤G′𝕀(rt∈Iρ⁡(n))\|v_{t}\|\leq G^{\prime}\,\ind(r_{t}\in I_{\rho(n)}). Consider sigma-algebras ℱtu=σ⁡(u1,…,ut−1)\mathcal{F}^{u}_{t}=\sigma(u_{1},...,u_{t-1}). Then, for all t∈[T]t\in[T], vt∈ℱt+1uv_{t}\in\mathcal{F}^{u}_{t+1} and 𝔼⁡[vt|ℱtu]=0\mathbb{E}[v_{t}|\mathcal{F}_{t}^{u}]=0. Therefore, it holds that

𝔼⁡[‖Mn‖2]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|M_{n}\right\|^{2}\right] =∑t=1T𝔼⁡[‖vt‖2]+2​∑t=1T∑s=t+1T𝔼⁡[⟨vt,vs⟩]\displaystyle=\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\left[\|v_{t}\|^{2}\right]+2\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\textstyle\sum_{s=t+1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\left[\langle{v_{t},v_{s}}\rangle\right]
≤∑t=1T(G′)2𝕀(rt∈Iρ⁡(n))+2∑t=1T∑s=t+1T𝔼[⟨vt,𝔼[vs|ℱsu]⟩]\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}(G^{\prime})^{2}\ind(r_{t}\in I_{\rho(n)})+2\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\textstyle\sum_{s=t+1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\left[\langle{v_{t},\mathbb{E}[v_{s}|\mathcal{F}^{u}_{s}]}\rangle\right]
=(G′)2​d~n⋆+0.\displaystyle=(G^{\prime})^{2}\,\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+0.

Combining these results and applying Jensen’s inequality, we prove the inequality

G​𝔼​[‖Γn‖]\displaystyle G\,\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\Gamma_{n}\right\|\right] ≤G2​d~n⋆+G​𝔼⁡[‖Mn‖2]≤G2​d~n⋆+G⁡(G+k​M/δn′)​d~n⋆\displaystyle\leq G^{2}\,\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+G\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[\left\|M_{n}\right\|^{2}]}\leq G^{2}\,\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+G(G+kM/\delta^{\prime}_{n})\sqrt{\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}
≤2​G2​d~n⋆+(G2​d~n⋆)1/2​(k​M/δn′)≤4​(G2​d~n⋆+(k​M/δn′)2).\displaystyle\leq 2G^{2}\,\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+(G^{2}\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n})^{1/2}(kM/\delta^{\prime}_{n})\leq 4(G^{2}\,\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+({kM}/{\delta^{\prime}_{n}})^{2}).

This concludes the proof of the lemma. ∎

Corollary 5.7 (Restated).

𝒲BCO​(ℬ)\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{BCO}}(\mathcal{B}), where (δt)t≥1(\delta_{t})_{t\geq 1} is set to either a round-dependent schedule δt=r​min⁡{1,ν​kt1/4}\delta_{t}=r\,\min\left\{1,\frac{\sqrt{\nu k}}{t^{1/4}}\right\} or a fixed schedule δt=r​min⁡{1,ν​kT1/4}\delta_{t}=r\,\min\left\{1,\frac{\sqrt{\nu k}}{T^{1/4}}\right\} and ℬ\mathcal{B} runs P-FTRL (4) with ηn=D/Gn+∑m=1n(σ~m⋆+(ν​k​r/δm′)2)\eta_{n}=\frac{D/G}{\sqrt{n+\sum_{m=1}^{n}(\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{m}+({\nu kr}/{\delta^{\prime}_{m}})^{2})}}, guarantees

The proof for a fixed schedule is the same as for a varying schedule, so we only present the latter. From Theorem E.3 and Lemma E.4, we have the following

≤D2ηT+5​G2​∑n=1Tηn​(d~n⋆+(ν​k​r/δn′)2)+G​D​Hη+6​G​D​δtotr.\displaystyle\leq\tfrac{D^{2}}{\eta_{T}}+5G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\left(\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+({\nu kr}/{\delta^{\prime}_{n}})^{2}\right)+GDH_{\eta}+\tfrac{6GD\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r}.

We bound the terms 1/ηT1/\eta_{T}, ∑n=1Tηn​(d~n⋆+(ν​k​r/δn′)2)\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\left(\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+({\nu kr}/{\delta^{\prime}_{n}})^{2}\right), and HηH_{\eta} separately.

  1. 1.

    As δT=mint∈[T]⁡δt\delta_{T}=\min_{t\in[T]}\delta_{t} and ∑n=1Tσ~n⋆=dtot\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}=d_{\textnormal{tot}}, it holds that

    1ηT=GD​T+∑m=1T(σ~m⋆+(ν​k​r/δm′)2)≤GD​(T+dtot+ν​k​rδT​T).\displaystyle\tfrac{1}{\eta_{T}}=\tfrac{G}{D}\sqrt{T+\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{T}(\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{m}+({\nu kr}/{\delta^{\prime}_{m}})^{2})}\leq\tfrac{G}{D}\left(\sqrt{T+d_{\textnormal{tot}}}+\tfrac{\nu kr}{\delta_{T}}\sqrt{T}\right).
  2. 2.

    As ∑m=1nd~m⋆≤∑m=1nσ~n⋆\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{n}\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{m}\leq\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{n}\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n} for all n∈[T]n\in[T] according to Fact C.2, we write

    ∑n=1Tηn​(d~n⋆+(ν​k​r/δn′)2)\displaystyle\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\left(\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+({\nu kr}/{\delta^{\prime}_{n}})^{2}\right) ≤DG​∑n=1Td~n⋆+(ν​k​r/δn′)2∑m=1n(d~m⋆+(ν​k​r/δm′)2)\displaystyle\leq\tfrac{D}{G}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\frac{\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+({\nu kr}/{\delta^{\prime}_{n}})^{2}}{\sqrt{\sum_{m=1}^{n}(\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{m}+({\nu kr}/{\delta^{\prime}_{m}})^{2})}}
    ≤2​DG​∑n=1T(d~n⋆+(ν​k​r/δn′)2)\displaystyle\leq\tfrac{2D}{G}\sqrt{\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}(\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+({\nu kr}/{\delta^{\prime}_{n}})^{2})}
    ≤2​DG​(T+dtot+(ν​k​r/δT)​T),\displaystyle\leq\tfrac{2D}{G}\left(\sqrt{T+d_{\textnormal{tot}}}+({\nu kr}/{\delta_{T}})\sqrt{T}\right),

    where the second inequality follows from Fact B.4 with Xn=d~n⋆+(ν​k​r/δn′)2X_{n}=\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+({\nu kr}/{\delta^{\prime}_{n}})^{2}.

  3. 3.

    For all n∈[T]n\in[T], it holds that

    ∑m=nn+σ~n⋆ηm≤∑m=nn+σ~n⋆D/Gm+∑k=nmσ~k⋆≤(a)∑m=0σ~n⋆D/G(m+1)+∑k=0m(σ~n⋆−k)≤(b)∑m=0σ~n⋆2​D/G(m+1)​(σ~n⋆+1)≤(c)4​DG,\displaystyle\textstyle\sum_{m=n}^{n+\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}}\eta_{m}\leq\textstyle\sum_{m=n}^{n+\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}}\tfrac{D/G}{\sqrt{m+\sum_{k=n}^{m}\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{k}}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{(a)}}}{{\leq}}\textstyle\sum_{m=0}^{\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}}\tfrac{D/G}{\sqrt{(m+1)+\sum_{k=0}^{m}(\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}-k)}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{(b)}}}{{\leq}}\textstyle\sum_{m=0}^{\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}}\tfrac{2D/G}{\sqrt{(m+1)(\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}+1)}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\text{(c)}}}{{\leq}}\tfrac{4D}{G},

    where (a) follows from Fact C.3, (b) applies inequality ∑k=0m(σ~n⋆−k)=(m+1)​(2​σ~n⋆−m)2≥(m+1)​σ~n⋆2\textstyle\sum_{k=0}^{m}(\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}-k)=\tfrac{(m+1)(2\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}-m)}{2}\geq\tfrac{(m+1)\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}}{2}, and (c) uses Fact B.4 to conclude ∑m=0σ~n⋆1m+1≤2​σ~n⋆+1\textstyle\sum_{m=0}^{\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}}\frac{1}{\sqrt{m+1}}\leq 2\sqrt{\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}+1}.

    Therefore, by Lemma D.6 and the bound on 1/ηT1/\eta_{T} above, we have

    Hη\displaystyle H_{\eta} ≤max⁡∑m=nn+σ~n⋆n∈[T]⁡ηmηT≤8​(T+dtot+(ν​k​r/δT)​T).\displaystyle\leq\tfrac{\max_{n\in[T]}{\sum_{m=n}^{n+\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}}\eta_{m}}}{\eta_{T}}\leq 8\left(\sqrt{T+d_{\textnormal{tot}}}+({\nu kr}/{\delta_{T}})\sqrt{T}\right).

Combining all these results, we have

R¯T​(x∗)=O⁡(G​D​(T+dtot+(ν​k​r/δT)​T+δtot/r)).\displaystyle\widebar{R}_{T}(x^{*})=O\left(GD\left(\sqrt{T+d_{\textnormal{tot}}}+({\nu kr}/{\delta_{T}})\sqrt{T}+\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}/r\right)\right).

Next, we provide the bounds on r/δTr/\delta_{T} and δtot/r\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}/r in order to derive the final bound. Trivially, it holds that r/δT≤max⁡{1,T1/4ν​k}{r}/{\delta_{T}}\leq\max\left\{1,\tfrac{T^{1/4}}{\sqrt{\nu k}}\right\}. Also, note that ∑t=1T1t1/4≤1+∫1Tx−1/4dx=1+43(T3/4−1)≤43T3/4\sum_{t=1}^{T}\frac{1}{t^{1/4}}\leq 1+\int_{1}^{T}x^{-1/4}\,dx=1+\frac{4}{3}(T^{3/4}-1)\leq\frac{4}{3}T^{3/4}, so that

δtot/r=∑t=1Tmin⁡{1,ν​kt1/4}≤∑t=1Tν​kt1/4≤43​T3/4​ν​k.\displaystyle\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}/r=\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\min\{1,\frac{\sqrt{\nu k}}{t^{1/4}}\}\leq\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\tfrac{\sqrt{\nu k}}{t^{1/4}}\leq\frac{4}{3}T^{3/4}\sqrt{\nu k}.

Thus, we have r/δT≤max⁡{1,T1/4ν​k}r/\delta_{T}\leq\max\left\{1,\tfrac{T^{1/4}}{\sqrt{\nu k}}\right\} and δtot/r≤43​T3/4​ν​k{\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}/{r}\leq\tfrac{4}{3}T^{3/4}\sqrt{\nu k}.

Finally, substituting the bounds for r/δTr/\delta_{T} and δtot/r\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}/r, we have

R¯T​(x∗)=O⁡(G​D​(T+dtot+T3/4​ν​k+T1/2​(ν​k)))=O⁡(G​D​(dtot+T3/4​ν​k)).\displaystyle\widebar{R}_{T}(x^{*})=O\left(GD\left(\sqrt{T+d_{\textnormal{tot}}}+T^{3/4}\sqrt{\nu k}+T^{1/2}(\nu{k})\right)\right)=O\left(GD\left(\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}}+T^{3/4}\sqrt{\nu k}\right)\right).

Corollary 5.8 (Restated).

Under λ\lambda-strong convexity (2.3), 𝒲BCO​(ℬ)\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{BCO}}(\mathcal{B}), where (δt)t≥1(\delta_{t})_{t\geq 1} is set to either a round-dependent schedule δt=r​min⁡{1,(ν2​k2​ln⁡tt)1/3}\delta_{t}=r\,\min\left\{1,(\tfrac{\nu^{2}{k}^{2}\ln t}{t})^{1/3}\right\} or a fixed schedule δt=r​min⁡{1,(ν2​k2​ln⁡TT)1/3}\delta_{t}=r\,\min\left\{1,(\tfrac{\nu^{2}{k}^{2}\ln T}{T})^{1/3}\right\} and ℬ\mathcal{B} runs P-FTRL (4) with ηn=1n​λ\eta_{n}=\tfrac{1}{n\lambda}, guarantees

R¯T​(x∗)\displaystyle\widebar{R}_{T}(x^{*}) =O⁡(G2λ​[min⁡{σmax​ln⁡T,dtot}+T2/3​(ln⁡T)1/3​(ν​k)2/3]).\displaystyle=O\!\left(\tfrac{G^{2}}{\lambda}\left[\min\{\sigma_{\textnormal{max}}\ln T,\,\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}}\}+T^{2/3}(\ln T)^{1/3}(\nu{k})^{2/3}\right]\right).

≤13​G2​∑n=1Tηn​(d~n⋆+(ν​k​r/δn′)2)+3​G​D​Hη+10​G​D​δtotr.\displaystyle\leq 13G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\left(\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+({\nu kr}/{\delta^{\prime}_{n}})^{2}\right)+3GDH_{\eta}+\tfrac{10GD\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r}.

We bound the terms ∑n=1Tηn​(d~n⋆+(ν​k​r/δn′)2)\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\left(\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+({\nu kr}/{\delta^{\prime}_{n}})^{2}\right) and HηH_{\eta} separately.

  1. 1.

  2. 2.

    Hη=∑n=1T(1−ηnηn−d~n⋆)=∑n=1Td~n⋆n≤min⁡{σmax​ln⁡(e​T), 2​dtot}.\displaystyle H_{\eta}=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}(1-\tfrac{\eta_{n}}{\eta_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}})=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\tfrac{\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}{n}\leq\min\left\{\sigma_{\textnormal{max}}\ln(eT),\,2\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}}\right\}.

Combining all these results and letting D≤2​GλD\leq\frac{2G}{\lambda} (see Fact B.1), we have

=O⁡(G2λ​(min⁡{σmax​ln⁡(T),dtot}+(ν​k​r/δT)2​ln⁡(T)+δtot/r)).\displaystyle=O\left(\tfrac{G^{2}}{\lambda}\left(\min\left\{\sigma_{\textnormal{max}}\ln(T),\,\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}}\right\}+({\nu kr}/{\delta_{T}})^{2}\ln(T)+\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}/r\right)\right).

=O⁡(G2λ​(min⁡{σmax​ln⁡(T),dtot}+T2/3​ln⁡(T)1/3​(ν​k)2/3)).\displaystyle=O\left(\tfrac{G^{2}}{\lambda}\left(\min\{\sigma_{\textnormal{max}}\ln(T),\,\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}}\}+T^{2/3}\ln(T)^{1/3}(\nu k)^{2/3}\right)\right).

Appendix F Skipping Scheme Proofs

Theorem 6.1 (Restated).

The regret RT​(u)R_{T}(u) of 𝒮skip​(𝒜){\mathcal{S}}_{\textnormal{skip}}(\mathcal{A}) against any comparator u∈𝒦u\in\mathcal{K} satisfies

RT​(u)\displaystyle R_{T}(u) ≤RT′​(u)+G​D​|Q∗|,\displaystyle\leq R^{\prime}_{T}(u)+GD|Q^{*}|,

where RT′​(u)=∑t=1T(ft′​(xt)−ft′​(u))R^{\prime}_{T}(u)=\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}(f^{\prime}_{t}(x_{t})-f^{\prime}_{t}(u)) is the regret of 𝒜\mathcal{A} on delayed OCO problem with losses and delays {ft′,dt′}t=1T\{f^{\prime}_{t},d^{\prime}_{t}\}_{t=1}^{T}. Moreover, it holds that

|Q∗|+∑t=1Tdt′\displaystyle|Q^{*}|+\sqrt{\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}d^{\prime}_{t}} =O⁡(minQ⊆[T]⁡{|Q|+∑t∉Qdt}).\displaystyle=O\left(\min_{Q\subseteq[T]}\left\{|Q|+\sqrt{\textstyle\sum_{t\notin Q}d_{t}}\right\}\right).
Proof.

The regret bound follows directly from the observation that each skipped round contributes at most G​DGD to the regret. Specifically, for all t∈[T]t\in[T], ft​(xt)−ft​(u)≤ft′​(xt)−ft′​(u)+G​D⋅𝕀(t∈Q∗)f_{t}(x_{t})-f_{t}(u)\leq f^{\prime}_{t}(x_{t})-f^{\prime}_{t}(u)+GD\cdot\ind(t\in Q^{*}). Summing over tt yields the first claim.

It remains to establish the second claim regarding the skipped set RR. We introduce additional notation: let StS_{t} denote the state of the tracking set SS at the start of round tt. By construction, dt′=∑s=1T𝕀(t∈Ss)≤dtd^{\prime}_{t}=\textstyle\sum_{s=1}^{T}\ind(t\in S_{s})\leq d_{t}. Then, dtot′=∑t=1Tdt′=∑t=1T|St|d_{\textnormal{tot}}^{\prime}=\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}d^{\prime}_{t}=\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}|S_{t}|. As 𝒟t=𝒟t−1+|St|\mathcal{D}_{t}=\mathcal{D}_{t-1}+|S_{t}|, it also holds that dtot′=𝒟Td_{\textnormal{tot}}^{\prime}=\mathcal{D}_{T}. Furthermore, by the preemption rule, round tt is not removed before round t+dt′−1t+d^{\prime}_{t}-1, which implies dt′≤𝒟t−1+1≤dtot′+1d^{\prime}_{t}\leq\sqrt{\mathcal{D}_{t-1}}+1\leq\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}^{\prime}}+1 for all t∈[T]t\in[T].

Part 1 (Bounding |Q∗||Q^{*}|): We show that |Q∗|≤2​dtot′|Q^{*}|\leq 2\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}^{\prime}}. Let Q∗={t1,…,t|Q∗|}Q^{*}=\{t_{1},\ldots,t_{|Q^{*}|}\} ordered by time of skipping. We claim that dts′≥s/2d^{\prime}_{t_{s}}\geq s/2 for all s∈[|Q∗|]s\in[|Q^{*}|]. Indeed, for each s∈[|Q∗|]s\in[|Q^{*}|],

dts′>𝒟ts+dts′=∑t=1Tmin⁡{dt′,ts+dts′−t}≥∑k=1sdtk′,\displaystyle d^{\prime}_{t_{s}}>\sqrt{\mathcal{D}_{t_{s}+d^{\prime}_{t_{s}}}}=\sqrt{\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\min\{d^{\prime}_{t},t_{s}+d^{\prime}_{t_{s}}-t\}}\geq\sqrt{\textstyle\sum_{k=1}^{s}d^{\prime}_{t_{k}}},

which rearranges to dts′≥1+1+4​∑k=1s−1dtk′2d^{\prime}_{t_{s}}\geq\frac{1+\sqrt{1+4\sum_{k=1}^{s-1}d^{\prime}_{t_{k}}}}{2} by solving the quadratic inequaltiy.

We proceed by induction. The base case gives dt1′≥1d^{\prime}_{t_{1}}\geq 1. Assuming dtk′≥k/2d^{\prime}_{t_{k}}\geq k/2 for all k<sk<s, we obtain

dts′≥1+1+4​∑k=1s−1k22=1+1+s⁡(s−1)2≥s2.\displaystyle d^{\prime}_{t_{s}}\geq\frac{1+\sqrt{1+4\sum_{k=1}^{s-1}\frac{k}{2}}}{2}=\frac{1+\sqrt{1+s(s-1)}}{2}\geq\frac{s}{2}.

Therefore, we have

dtot′≥∑s=1|Q∗|dts′≥∑s=1|Q∗|s2=|Q∗|​(|Q∗|+1)4≥|Q∗|2.\displaystyle\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}^{\prime}}\geq\sqrt{\textstyle\sum_{s=1}^{|Q^{*}|}d^{\prime}_{t_{s}}}\geq\sqrt{\textstyle\sum_{s=1}^{|Q^{*}|}\frac{s}{2}}=\sqrt{\tfrac{|Q^{*}|(|Q^{*}|+1)}{4}}\geq\frac{|Q^{*}|}{2}.

Part 2 (Bounding dtot′d_{\textnormal{tot}}^{\prime}): Fix an arbitrary Q⊆[T]Q\subseteq[T]. Using dt′≤dtot′+1d^{\prime}_{t}\leq\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}^{\prime}}+1 for all tt, we have

∑t∉Qdt≥∑t∉Qdt′≥max⁡{0,dtot′−|Q|​(dtot′+1)}.\displaystyle\textstyle\sum_{t\notin Q}d_{t}\geq\textstyle\sum_{t\notin Q}d^{\prime}_{t}\geq\max\left\{0,\,d_{\textnormal{tot}}^{\prime}-|Q|(\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}^{\prime}}+1)\right\}.

Consequently, we can write

|Q|+∑t∉Qdt\displaystyle|Q|+\sqrt{\textstyle\sum_{t\notin Q}d_{t}} ≥minq≥0⁡{q+max⁡{0,dtot′−q⁡(dtot′+1)}}\displaystyle\geq\min_{q\geq 0}\left\{q+\sqrt{\max\{0,\,d_{\textnormal{tot}}^{\prime}-q(\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}^{\prime}}+1)\}}\right\}
≥min⁡{dtot′−1,minq∈[0,dtot′−1]⁡{q+dtot′−q⁡(dtot′+1)}}\displaystyle\geq\min\left\{\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}^{\prime}}-1,\,\min_{q\in[0,\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}^{\prime}}-1]}\left\{q+\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}^{\prime}-q(\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}^{\prime}}+1)}\right\}\right\}
=dtot′−1.\displaystyle=\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}^{\prime}}-1.

Combining both parts and minimizing over Q⊆[T]Q\subseteq[T], we conclude

|Q∗|+∑t=1Tdt′≤2​dtot′+dtot′=3​dtot′=O⁡(minQ⊆[T]⁡{|Q|+∑t∉Qdt}),\displaystyle|Q^{*}|+\sqrt{\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}d^{\prime}_{t}}\leq 2\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}^{\prime}}+\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}^{\prime}}=3\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}^{\prime}}=O\left(\min_{Q\subseteq[T]}\left\{|Q|+\sqrt{\textstyle\sum_{t\notin Q}d_{t}}\right\}\right),

completing the proof. ∎

Corollary 6.2 (Restated).

Under the conditions of Corollaries 5.3 and 5.7, applying the skipping wrapper yields:

RT​(x∗)=O⁡(G​D​[minQ⊆[T]⁡{|Q|+∑t∉Qdt}+T]),\displaystyle R_{T}(x^{*})=O\bigg(\!GD\bigg[\!\min_{Q\subseteq[T]}\Big\{\!|Q|\!+\!\sqrt{\!\textstyle\sum_{t\notin Q}d_{t}\!}\Big\}\!+\!\sqrt{T}\bigg]\!\bigg),
R¯T​(x∗)=O⁡(G​D​[minQ⊆[T]⁡{|Q|+∑t∉Qdt}+T34​ν​k]),\displaystyle\widebar{R}_{T}(x^{*})=O\bigg(\!GD\bigg[\!\min_{Q\subseteq[T]}\Big\{\!|Q|\!+\!\sqrt{\!\textstyle\sum_{t\notin Q}d_{t}\!}\Big\}\!+\!T^{\frac{3}{4}}\sqrt{\!\nu k}\bigg]\!\bigg),

for 𝒮skip​(𝒲OCO​(ℬ)){\mathcal{S}}_{\textnormal{skip}}(\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{OCO}}(\mathcal{B})) and 𝒮skip​(𝒲BCO​(ℬ)){\mathcal{S}}_{\textnormal{skip}}(\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{BCO}}(\mathcal{B})), respectively.

Appendix G Bandit Convex Optimization with Two-Point Delayed Feedback

In this section, we extend the analysis of BCO with delayed feedback (see Section 2) to the two-point feedback setting Agarwal et al. (2010). In each round tt, the player selects a pair of points xt1,xt2∈𝒦x_{t}^{1},x_{t}^{2}\in\mathcal{K} (the same domain as Section 2), incurs loss 12​(ft​(xt1)+ft​(xt2))\tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(f_{t}(x_{t}^{1})+f_{t}(x_{t}^{2})\bigr), and later receives the delayed feedback (t,ft​(xt1),ft​(xt2))(t,f_{t}(x_{t}^{1}),f_{t}(x_{t}^{2})) in round t+dtt+d_{t}.

The two-point regret against a comparator u∈𝒦u\in\mathcal{K} is defined as RT2p​(u)=∑t=1T(12​(ft​(xt1)+ft​(xt2))−ft​(u))R^{\textnormal{2p}}_{T}(u)=\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}(\frac{1}{2}(f_{t}(x^{1}_{t})+f_{t}(x^{2}_{t}))-f_{t}(u)) and its expectation as R¯T2p​(u)=𝔼⁡[RT2p​(u)]\widebar{R}^{\textnormal{2p}}_{T}(u)=\mathbb{E}[R^{\textnormal{2p}}_{T}(u)]. Letting x∗∈argminx∈𝒦∑t=1Tft(x)x^{*}\in\argmin_{x\in\mathcal{K}}\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}f_{t}(x) denote the best action in hindsight, the goal is to minimize R¯T2p​(x∗)\widebar{R}^{\textnormal{2p}}_{T}(x^{*}).

Preliminaries on two-point gradient estimation.

We briefly review the standard two-point gradient estimator. By Theorem 5.5, the gradient of the δ\delta-smoothed loss fδf^{\delta} admits a spherical expectation representation; by symmetry of u∼Unif​(𝕊k−1)u\sim\textnormal{Unif}(\mathbb{S}^{k-1}), this can be written in the two-point form

∇fδ​(x)=𝔼u∼Unif​(𝕊k−1)​[k2​δ​(f⁡(x+δ​u)−f⁡(x−δ​u))​u].\nabla f^{\delta}(x)=\mathbb{E}_{u\sim\textnormal{Unif}(\mathbb{S}^{k-1})}\!\left[\tfrac{k}{2\delta}\bigl(f(x+\delta u)-f(x-\delta u)\bigr)u\right].

Accordingly, the estimator k2​δ​(f⁡(x+δ​u)−f⁡(x−δ​u))​u\tfrac{k}{2\delta}\bigl(f(x+\delta u)-f(x-\delta u)\bigr)u is unbiased for ∇fδ​(x)\nabla f^{\delta}(x) (Agarwal et al., 2010; Shamir, 2017). Moreover, unlike the one-point estimator, its second moment does not scale with 1/δ1/\delta, as captured by the following lemma.

Lemma G.1 (Lemma 5, Shamir (2017)).

There exists a numerical constant c>0c>0 such that for every GG-Lipschitz function f:𝒦→ℝf:\mathcal{K}\to\mathbb{R}, δ∈(0,r]\delta\in(0,r], and x∈(1−δ/r)​𝒦x\in(1-\delta/r)\mathcal{K}, it holds that

𝔼u∼Unif​(𝕊k−1)​[‖k2​δ​(f⁡(x+δ​u)−f⁡(x−δ​u))​u‖2]≤c​k​G2.\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{u\sim\textnormal{Unif}(\mathbb{S}^{k-1})}\!\left[\left\|\tfrac{k}{2\delta}\bigl(f(x+\delta u)-f(x-\delta u)\bigr)u\right\|^{2}\right]\leq c\,kG^{2}.

Two-point Delayed BCO via Drift-Penalized OLO.

The wrapper 𝒲2p-BCO\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{2p-BCO}} (Algorithm 4) follows the structure of 𝒲BCO\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{BCO}}, with two-point gradient estimates instead of single-point estimates. As before, the algorithm takes as input a non-increasing sequence of smoothing parameters (δt)t≥1⊂(0,r](\delta_{t})_{t\geq 1}\subset(0,r] fixed in advance. In round tt, given the current base-prediction yt=z¯y_{t}=\widebar{z} from ℬ\mathcal{B}, the algorithm samples an exploration direction ut∼Unif​(𝕊k−1)u_{t}\sim\textnormal{Unif}(\mathbb{S}^{k-1}) and predicts xt1=xt+δt​utx^{1}_{t}=x_{t}+\delta_{t}u_{t}, xt2=xt−δt​utx^{2}_{t}=x_{t}-\delta_{t}u_{t} for xt=(1−δt/r)​ytx_{t}=(1-\delta_{t}/r)y_{t}. Upon receiving observations (s,fs​(xs1),fs​(xs2))(s,f_{s}(x^{1}_{s}),f_{s}(x^{2}_{s})), it constructs the two-point gradient estimate g^sδ=k2​δs​(fs​(xs1)−fs​(xs2))​us\widehat{g}^{\delta}_{s}=\tfrac{k}{2\delta_{s}}(f_{s}(x^{1}_{s})-f_{s}(x^{2}_{s}))u_{s}. This estimate satisfies 𝔼⁡[g^tδ∣xt]=∇ftδ​(xt)\mathbb{E}[\widehat{g}^{\delta}_{t}\mid x_{t}]=\nabla f^{\delta}_{t}(x_{t}) with reduced variance compared to single-point estimation.

The analysis follows the same structure as for 𝒲BCO\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{BCO}}. The algorithm updates ℬ\mathcal{B} sequentially on tuples (g^~nδ,d~n⋆,σ~n⋆)(\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{n},\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n},\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}) for n∈[T]n\in[T], where g^~nδ=k2​δ~n​(f~n​(x~n1)−f~n​(x~n2))​u~n\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{n}=\tfrac{k}{2\widetilde{\delta}_{n}}(\widetilde{f}_{n}(\widetilde{x}^{1}_{n})-\widetilde{f}_{n}(\widetilde{x}^{2}_{n}))\widetilde{u}_{n}, producing base-predictions znz_{n} that yield predictions x~n1=x~n+δ~n​u~n\widetilde{x}^{1}_{n}=\widetilde{x}_{n}+\widetilde{\delta}_{n}\widetilde{u}_{n} and x~n2=x~n−δ~n​u~n\widetilde{x}^{2}_{n}=\widetilde{x}_{n}-\widetilde{\delta}_{n}\widetilde{u}_{n} for x~n=(1−δ~n/r)​y~n\widetilde{x}_{n}=(1-\widetilde{\delta}_{n}/r)\widetilde{y}_{n} and y~n=zn−d~n⋆\widetilde{y}_{n}=z_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}. The following theorem bounds the expected two-point regret of 𝒲2p-BCO​(ℬ)\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{2p-BCO}}(\mathcal{B}) in terms of the drift-penalized regret of ℬ\mathcal{B}, with an additional bias of order δtot=∑t=1Tδt\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\delta_{t} due to smoothing.

Theorem G.2 (Regret of Algorithm 4).

For any base-algorithm ℬ\mathcal{B}, non-increasing sequence (δt)t≥1⊂(0,r](\delta_{t})_{t\geq 1}\subset(0,r], and comparator u∈𝒦u\in\mathcal{K}, 𝒲2p-BCO​(ℬ)\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{2p-BCO}}(\mathcal{B}) guarantees

R¯T2p​(u)\displaystyle\widebar{R}^{\textnormal{2p}}_{T}(u) ≤𝔼⁡[ℜTdrift​(u,G)]+7​G​R​δtotr,\displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}\left[\mathfrak{R}^{\textnormal{drift}}_{T}(u;G)\right]+\tfrac{7GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r},

where ℜTdrift​(u,W)\mathfrak{R}^{\textnormal{drift}}_{T}(u;W) is the drift-penalized regret (3) of ℬ\mathcal{B} for loss vectors cn=g^~nδc_{n}=\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{n} and lags λn=d~n⋆\lambda_{n}=\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}.

Under λ\lambda-strong convexity (2.3), it further holds that

R¯2p​(u)\displaystyle\widebar{R}^{\textnormal{2p}}(u) ≤𝔼⁡[ℜTdrift​(u,3​G)−λ2​∑n=1T‖zn−u‖2]+11​G​R​δtotr.\displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathfrak{R}^{\textnormal{drift}}_{T}(u;3G)\!-\!\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\!\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\|z_{n}\!-\!u\|^{2}\right]\!+\!\tfrac{11GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r}.
Proof.

The argument follows the proof of Theorem 5.6. Here the played center xtx_{t} plays the role of yty_{t} in that theorem, so the same steps bound ∑t=1T(ft​(xt)−ft​(u))\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\bigl(f_{t}(x_{t})-f_{t}(u)\bigr). It remains to relate the two-point loss to the center loss: by GG-Lipschitzness,

|12​(ft​(xt1)+ft​(xt2))−ft​(xt)|≤G2​(‖xt1−xt‖+‖xt2−xt‖)=G​δt.\left|\tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(f_{t}(x_{t}^{1})+f_{t}(x_{t}^{2})\bigr)-f_{t}(x_{t})\right|\leq\tfrac{G}{2}\bigl(\|x_{t}^{1}-x_{t}\|+\|x_{t}^{2}-x_{t}\|\bigr)=G\delta_{t}.

Summing over tt yields |∑t=1T[12​(ft​(xt1)+ft​(xt2))−ft​(xt)]|≤G​δtot≤G​R​δtotr\left|\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left[\tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(f_{t}(x_{t}^{1})+f_{t}(x_{t}^{2})\bigr)-f_{t}(x_{t})\right]\right|\leq G\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}\leq\frac{GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r}, which gives the claim. ∎

Selecting an appropriate smoothing sequence (δt)t=1T(\delta_{t})_{t=1}^{T} and instantiating ℬ\mathcal{B} with P-FTRL (4) yields concrete guarantees.

Corollary G.3.

𝒲2p-BCO​(ℬ)\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{2p-BCO}}(\mathcal{B}) with δt=rt\delta_{t}=\frac{r}{\sqrt{t}}, where ℬ\mathcal{B} runs P-FTRL (4) with ηn=D/Gn​k+∑m=1nσ~m⋆\eta_{n}=\tfrac{D/G}{\sqrt{nk+\sum_{m=1}^{n}\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{m}}}, guarantees

R¯T2p​(x∗)=O⁡(G​D​[dtot+T​k]).\displaystyle\widebar{R}^{\textnormal{2p}}_{T}(x^{*})=O\left(GD\left[\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}}+\sqrt{Tk}\right]\right).

Composing with the skipping scheme, 𝒮skip​(𝒲2p-BCO​(ℬ)){\mathcal{S}}_{\textnormal{skip}}(\mathcal{W}_{\text{2p-BCO}}(\mathcal{B})) gets R¯T2p​(x∗)=O⁡(G​D​[minQ⊆[T]⁡{|Q|+(∑t∉Qdt)12}+T​k])\widebar{R}^{\textnormal{2p}}_{T}(x^{*})=O(GD[\min_{Q\subseteq[T]}\{|Q|+(\sum_{t\notin Q}d_{t})^{\frac{1}{2}}\}+\sqrt{Tk}]).

Corollary G.4.

Under λ\lambda-strong convexity (2.3), 𝒲2p-BCO​(ℬ)\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{2p-BCO}}(\mathcal{B}) with δt=rt\delta_{t}=\frac{r}{t}, where ℬ\mathcal{B} runs P-FTRL (4) with ηn=1n​λ\eta_{n}=\frac{1}{n\lambda}, guarantees

R¯T2p​(x∗)=O⁡(G2λ​[min⁡{σmax​ln⁡(T),dtot}+k​ln⁡T]).\displaystyle\widebar{R}^{\textnormal{2p}}_{T}(x^{*})=O\left(\tfrac{G^{2}}{\lambda}\left[\min\{\sigma_{\textnormal{max}}\ln(T),\,\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}}\}+k\ln T\right]\right).

G.1 Proofs of Corollaries G.3 and G.4

Theorem G.5.

𝒲2p-BCO​(ℬ)\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{2p-BCO}}(\mathcal{B}), where ℬ\mathcal{B} executes P-FTRL (4) updates, guarantees that in the

general convex convex:R¯T2p​(u)\displaystyle\text{general convex convex}\colon\,\widebar{R}^{\textnormal{2p}}_{T}(u) ≤D22​ηT+∑n=1Tηn​(G​𝔼​[‖Γn‖]+G2​c​k)+G​D​Hη+7​G​R​δtotr,\displaystyle\leq\tfrac{D^{2}}{2\eta_{T}}+\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\left(G\,\mathbb{E}[\|\Gamma_{n}\|]+G^{2}\,ck\right)+GDH_{\eta}+\tfrac{7GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r},

+∑n=1Tηn(3G𝔼[∥Γn∥]+G2ck)+3GDHη+11​G​R​δtotr,\displaystyle+\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\left(3G\,\mathbb{E}[\|\Gamma_{n}\|]+G^{2}\,ck\right)+3GDH_{\eta}+\tfrac{11GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r},

where Γn=∑m=n−d~n⋆n−1g^~mδ\Gamma_{n}=\textstyle\sum_{m=n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}^{n-1}\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{m}, Hη=∑n=1T(1−ηn/ηn−d~n⋆)H_{\eta}=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}(1-\eta_{n}/{\eta_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}}), and cc is the constant from Lemma G.1.

Follows identically to Theorem E.3, using the bound 𝔼⁡[‖g^~nδ‖2]≤c​k​G2\mathbb{E}[\|\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{n}\|^{2}]\leq c\,kG^{2} from Lemma G.1. ∎

Lemma G.6.

For the constant cc from Lemma G.1, Γn=∑m=n−d~n⋆n−1g^~mδ\Gamma_{n}=\textstyle\sum_{m=n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}^{n-1}\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{m} satisfies

𝔼⁡[‖Γn‖2]≤2​G​(d~n⋆+c​k).\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\Gamma_{n}\right\|_{2}\right]\leq 2G\,(\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+ck).
Proof.

Note that ‖g~nδ‖≤G\|\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{n}\|\leq G, 𝔼⁡[g^~nδ]=g~nδ\mathbb{E}[\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{n}]=\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{n} by Theorem 5.5 and 𝔼⁡[‖g^~nδ−g~nδ‖2]≤c​k​G2\mathbb{E}[\|\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{n}-\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{n}\|^{2}]\leq ckG^{2} by Lemma G.1.

With probability one, we write

‖Γn‖≤∑m=n−d~n⋆n−1∥g~mδ∥+∥∑m=n−d~n⋆n−1(g^~mδ−g~mδ)⏟=:Mn∥≤Gd~n⋆+∥Mn∥.\displaystyle\left\|\Gamma_{n}\right\|\leq\textstyle\sum_{m=n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}^{n-1}\|\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{m}\|+\|\underbrace{\textstyle\sum_{m=n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}^{n-1}(\widetilde{\widehat{g}}^{\delta}_{m}-\widetilde{g}^{\delta}_{m})}_{=:M_{n}}\|\leq G\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+\|M_{n}\|.

Let vt=(g^tδ−gtδ)𝕀(rt∈Iρ⁡(n))v_{t}=(\widehat{g}^{\delta}_{t}-g^{\delta}_{t})\ind(r_{t}\in I_{\rho(n)}), so that Mn=∑t=1TvtM_{n}=\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}v_{t}, 𝔼⁡[vt]=0\mathbb{E}[v_{t}]=0, and 𝔼[∥vt∥2]≤ckG2𝕀(rt∈Iρ⁡(n))\mathbb{E}[\|v_{t}\|^{2}]\leq ckG^{2}\ind(r_{t}\in I_{\rho(n)}).

𝔼⁡[‖Mn‖2]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|M_{n}\right\|^{2}\right] =∑t=1T𝔼⁡[‖vt‖2]+2​∑t=1T∑s=t+1T𝔼⁡[⟨vt,vs⟩]\displaystyle=\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\left[\|v_{t}\|^{2}\right]+2\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\textstyle\sum_{s=t+1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\left[\langle{v_{t},v_{s}}\rangle\right]
≤∑t=1TckG2𝕀(rt∈Iρ⁡(n))+2∑t=1T∑s=t+1T𝔼[⟨vt,𝔼[vs|ℱsu]⟩]\displaystyle\leq\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}ckG^{2}\ind(r_{t}\in I_{\rho(n)})+2\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\textstyle\sum_{s=t+1}^{T}\mathbb{E}\left[\langle{v_{t},\mathbb{E}[v_{s}|\mathcal{F}^{u}_{s}]}\rangle\right]
=c​k​G2​d~n⋆+0.\displaystyle=c\,kG^{2}\,\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+0.

Combining these results and applying Jensen’s inequality, we prove the inequality

𝔼⁡[‖Γn‖]≤G​d~n⋆+𝔼⁡[‖Mn‖2]≤G​d~n⋆+G​(c​k)1/2​d~n⋆≤2​G​(d~n⋆+c​k).\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\Gamma_{n}\right\|\right]\leq G\,\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[\left\|M_{n}\right\|^{2}]}\leq G\,\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+G(ck)^{1/2}\sqrt{\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}\leq 2G\,(\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+ck).

This concludes the proof of the lemma. ∎

Corollary G.4 (Restated).

𝒲2p-BCO​(ℬ)\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{2p-BCO}}(\mathcal{B}) with δt=rt\delta_{t}=\frac{r}{\sqrt{t}}, where ℬ\mathcal{B} runs P-FTRL (4) with ηn=D/Gn​k+∑m=1nσ~m⋆\eta_{n}=\tfrac{D/G}{\sqrt{nk+\sum_{m=1}^{n}\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{m}}}, guarantees

R¯T2p​(x∗)=O⁡(G​D​[dtot+T​k]).\displaystyle\widebar{R}^{\textnormal{2p}}_{T}(x^{*})=O\left(GD\left[\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}}+\sqrt{Tk}\right]\right).

Composing with the skipping scheme, 𝒮skip​(𝒲2p-BCO​(ℬ)){\mathcal{S}}_{\textnormal{skip}}(\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{2p-BCO}}(\mathcal{B})) gets R¯T2p​(x∗)=O⁡(G​D​[minQ⊆[T]⁡{|Q|+(∑t∉Qdt)12}+T​k])\widebar{R}^{\textnormal{2p}}_{T}(x^{*})=O(GD[\min_{Q\subseteq[T]}\{|Q|+(\sum_{t\notin Q}d_{t})^{\frac{1}{2}}\}+\sqrt{Tk}]).

From Theorem G.5 and Lemma G.6, we have the following

≤D2ηT+5​(c+1)​G2​∑n=1Tηn​(d~n⋆+k)+G​D​Hη+7​G​D​δtotr.\displaystyle\leq\tfrac{D^{2}}{\eta_{T}}+5(c+1)G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}(\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+k)+GDH_{\eta}+\tfrac{7GD\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r}.

We bound the terms 1/ηT1/\eta_{T}, ∑n=1Tηn​(d~n⋆+k)\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}(\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+k), and HηH_{\eta} separately.

    As ∑n=1Tσ~n⋆=dtot\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\widetilde{\sigma}^{\star}_{n}=d_{\textnormal{tot}} according to Theorem 3.4, it holds that

    ≤2​DG​∑n=1T(d~n⋆+k)\displaystyle\leq\tfrac{2D}{G}\sqrt{\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}(\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+k)}
    ≤2​DG​(dtot+T​k),\displaystyle\leq\tfrac{2D}{G}\left(\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}}+\sqrt{Tk}\right),

    where the second inequality follows from Fact B.4 with Xn=d~n⋆+kX_{n}=\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+k.

For our choice of δt\delta_{t}, we have δtot/r=∑t=1T1t1/2≤2​T\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}/r=\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\tfrac{1}{t^{1/2}}\leq 2\sqrt{T}, which follows immediately from Fact B.4.

Combining all these results, we have

R¯T2p​(x∗)=O⁡(G​D​[dtot+T​k]).\displaystyle\widebar{R}^{\textnormal{2p}}_{T}(x^{*})=O\left(GD\left[\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}}+\sqrt{Tk}\right]\right).

The result for the skipping scheme follows from Theorem 6.1. ∎

Corollary G.4 (Restated).

Under λ\lambda-strong convexity (2.3), 𝒲2p-BCO​(ℬ)\mathcal{W}_{\textnormal{2p-BCO}}(\mathcal{B}) with δt=rt\delta_{t}=\frac{r}{t}, where ℬ\mathcal{B} runs P-FTRL (4) with ηn=1n​λ\eta_{n}=\frac{1}{n\lambda}, guarantees

R¯T2p​(x∗)=O⁡(G2λ​[min⁡{σmax​ln⁡T,dtot}+k​ln⁡T]).\displaystyle\widebar{R}^{\textnormal{2p}}_{T}(x^{*})=O\left(\tfrac{G^{2}}{\lambda}\left[\min\{\sigma_{\textnormal{max}}\ln T,\,\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}}\}+k\ln T\right]\right).
Proof.

From Theorem G.5 and Lemma G.6, noting that 1/ηn−1/ηn−1−λ=01/\eta_{n}-1/\eta_{n-1}-\lambda=0, we have the following

R¯T2p​(x∗)\displaystyle\widebar{R}^{\textnormal{2p}}_{T}(x^{*}) ≤0+∑n=1Tηn​(3​G​𝔼​[‖Γn‖]+G2​c​k)+3​G​D​Hη+11​G​R​δtotr,\displaystyle\leq 0+\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}\left(3G\,\mathbb{E}[\|\Gamma_{n}\|]+G^{2}\,ck\right)+3GDH_{\eta}+\tfrac{11GR\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r},
≤13​(c+1)​G2​∑n=1Tηn​(d~n⋆+k)+3​G​D​Hη+11​G​D​δtotr.\displaystyle\leq 13(c+1)G^{2}\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}(\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+k)+3GDH_{\eta}+\tfrac{11GD\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}}{r}.

We bound the terms ∑n=1Tηn​(d~n⋆+k)\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}(\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+k) and HηH_{\eta} separately.

  1. 1.

    Using Fact C.4 for dual delays d~n⋆\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n} and Fact B.3, we write

    ∑n=1Tηn​(d~n⋆+k)\displaystyle\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\eta_{n}(\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}+k) ≤1λ​min⁡{σmax​ln⁡(e​T), 2​dtot}+1λ​k​ln⁡(e​T).\displaystyle\leq\tfrac{1}{\lambda}\min\left\{\sigma_{\textnormal{max}}\ln(eT),\,2\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}}\right\}+\tfrac{1}{\lambda}k\ln(eT).
  2. 2.

    Substituting learning rate values into HηH_{\eta} and applying Fact C.4 for dual delays d~n⋆\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n} yields

    Hη=∑n=1T(1−ηnηn−d~n⋆)=∑n=1Td~n⋆n≤min⁡{σmax​ln⁡(e​T), 2​dtot}.\displaystyle H_{\eta}=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}(1-\tfrac{\eta_{n}}{\eta_{n-\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}})=\textstyle\sum_{n=1}^{T}\tfrac{\widetilde{d}^{\star}_{n}}{n}\leq\min\left\{\sigma_{\textnormal{max}}\ln(eT),\,2\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}}\right\}.

For our choice of δt\delta_{t}, we have δtot/r=∑t=1T1t≤ln⁡(e​T)\delta_{\textnormal{tot}}/r=\textstyle\sum_{t=1}^{T}\tfrac{1}{t}\leq\ln(eT), which follows immediately from Fact B.3.

Combining all these results and letting D≤2​GλD\leq\frac{2G}{\lambda} (see Fact B.1), we have

R¯T2p​(x∗)\displaystyle\widebar{R}^{\textnormal{2p}}_{T}(x^{*}) =O⁡(G2λ​[min⁡{σmax​ln⁡T,dtot}+k​ln⁡T]).\displaystyle=O\left(\tfrac{G^{2}}{\lambda}\left[\min\{\sigma_{\textnormal{max}}\ln T,\,\sqrt{d_{\textnormal{tot}}}\}+k\ln T\right]\right).

This concludes the proof of the corollary. ∎
